title: Man Utd vs Man City: Six Subplots That Could Decide the Manchester Derby | Opta Analyst
author: Ryan Benson
content:
Ahead of Sunday’s Manchester derby at Old Trafford in the Premier League, we identify six elements that could be decisive.
Sunday’s Manchester derby will have a slightly different feel.
For the first time in over 10 years, Pep Guardiola won’t be in the Manchester City dugout for it, with this to be Enzo Maresca’s bow in the derby.
The Italian has enjoyed a decent start in charge, winning each of his first three Premier League games, but this will be his first major top-flight test, and against a Manchester United side already frustrated to be playing catch-up.
Here, we look at several facets that may decide the outcome of the contest.
City Give Up Chances
Having brushed off that rather chastening 3-0 Community Shield defeat to Arsenal, Manchester City have started the season well in terms of results, racking up three wins in the Premier League and beginning their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 success at Porto.
Beyond the results, though, City haven’t looked infallible.
United will take particular encouragement from City’s 1-0 win over Coventry last weekend.
![Man City vs Coventry xG race](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/man-city-vs-coventry-xg-race-1024x576.jpeg)
City had plenty of joy in attack, sure, wasting several opportunities. But at the other end they were fortunate to not concede. Taiwo Awoniyi spurned a gift of chance early on; Jack Rudoni’s close-range header was saved by Gianluigi Donnarumma; Ellis Simms was denied by the keeper’s face late on.
Across their five games in all competitions this season, City have afforded their opponents 3+ ‘big chances’ (opportunities from which a team would ordinarily be expected to score) on three occasions, the exceptions being Bournemouth (1) and Porto (0).
But even against Porto, the Portuguese side may not have managed a single shot on target, but there were numerous moments when they worried City. The main issues for Porto were poor final passes and difficulty staying onside; they were caught offside seven times having only done so five times across their previous seven games in major European competition.
Given the upheaval City went through over the summer, it’s only natural that they have imperfections, but the signs suggest they will afford United – who, heading into the weekend, rank top for shots (68) and second for xG (7.3) in the Premier League this term – chances on Sunday.
United’s Latest Nemesis
Erling Haaland scores lots of goals against Man Utd.
Erling Haaland scores lots of goals during the opening weeks of the season.
Highlighting Haaland as a probable threat to United isn’t a hot take, we freely admit, but when considering potentially decisive aspects ahead of the derby, how could we ignore him?
He’s a man for the big occasion, so unsurprisingly he boasts a fine record in the derby.
In seven Premier League games against United, Haaland has scored eight goals. Only Mohamed Salah (13) and Alan Shearer (10) have netted more against them in the competition.
![Erling Haaland Premier League Goals vs Man Utd](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/erling-haaland-premier-league-goals-vs-man-utd-1024x768.jpeg)
Haaland has only scored more Premier League goals against Crystal Palace, Wolves (both 10) and West Ham (11), and his 7.1 xG vs United is his third best against a single opponent.
On top of that, Haaland typically starts seasons well, as the chart below from his first four Premier League seasons reflects.
August (24) and September (16) are his two most prolific months of the year for Premier League goals, and he heads into the weekend having scored in each of his past three games in all competitions.
If there’s one omen United fans can look to, it’s that Haaland has scored just the two goals at Old Trafford in the league – he’s also only played three times there, though, so it’s hardly a dismal record.
Either way, keep him quiet and United’s chances improve considerably. If that wasn’t obvious.
Kobbie Mainoo vs Elliot Anderson
Those with an interest in England matters will likely have an eye on two of the national team’s most promising young midfielders, who will go head-to-head on Sunday.
Elliot Anderson had a big summer, playing an important role for England as they finished third at the World Cup, and securing a massive move to City.
Kobbie Mainoo, on the other hand, was the only outfield player in the England squad not to play a single minute in North America, a fact that mystified United fans who adore him.
But Mainoo has enjoyed an excellent start to the new domestic season. Previously, some had doubts about his physical capacity and defensive awareness, but he seems to have made strides under Carrick and taken his game to another level.
He’s harder to knock off the ball, tougher in duels, and just seems to be everywhere in United’s midfield.
His 68.2% success rate in duels is the sixth best among midfielders to play more than 90 minutes this season, while his 10.1 possession regains per 90 puts him second among the same group. He remains dependable as ever on the ball, too, ranking 6/28 for pass completion rate under pressure (90.3%) among defensive/central midfielders to tally at least 50 such passes.
![Kobbie Mainoo passes under pressure 2026-27](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kobbie-mainoo-passes-under-pressure-2026-27-1024x768.jpeg)
Mainoo then controlled proceedings against Sabah in the Champions League on Thursday, having the most touches (93), passes (83) and accurate passes (81) despite coming off after 64 minutes.
Of course, Anderson is a quality player in his own right and did little wrong during the World Cup. He’s also enjoyed a seamless start to life at City, quickly taking over command of their midfield from the departed Rodri.
He’s combative, an excellent passer and a confident carrier. For instance, among midfielders to play more than 90 minutes this term, he ranks seventh for tackle attempts per 90 (3.1) and top for passes per 90 (121.4), progressive carries per 90 (19.5) and line-breaking passes (76).
![Elliot Anderson - line-breaking passes 2026-27](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/elliot-anderson-line-breaking-passes-2026-27-1024x768.jpeg)
For Anderson, Sunday will be his first blockbuster Premier League game at City, a chance to position himself as the top flight’s leading midfielder. Whereas Mainoo, who’s remained quiet about any possible World Cup frustration, has the opportunity to let his feet do the talking against a direct positional rival.
It ought to make for compelling viewing.
Bruno Fernandes or Rayan Cherki: Who Will Be Most Influential?
If the Mainoo v Anderson duel could determine which side has the ascendancy in midfield, the outcome of the match may be swung by whomever of Bruno Fernandes and Rayan Cherki is able to exert the most influence.
Fernandes and Cherki were the Premier League’s two standout creators in 2025-26.
While Fernandes’ totals largely dwarfed those of his rival, when adjusted to a per-90 basis, their respective outputs were a lot closer.
![Bruno Fernandes vs Rayan Cherki 2025-26](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/bruno-fernandes-vs-rayan-cherki-2025-26-1-1024x1024.png)
One metric where Cherki actually came out comfortably on top was expected assists (xA) per 90 (0.44 to Fernandes’ 0.36), highlighting how frequently the Frenchman found teammates in dangerous positions.
Cherki’s 2026-27 has begun impressively as well. Clearly we are still talking about small sample sizes here, but his 0.69 xA per 90 is easily the highest of any player to feature for at least 90 mins this term, and he’s averaged 5.1 chances created per 90 across his 175 minutes on the pitch.
He has two assists already, both against Bournemouth, and he also scored twice in the win over Crystal Palace. He’s going into the derby a man in form.
Fernandes’ influence has been felt slightly less so far this term from a creative perspective, though that’s probably partly because United aren’t quite so reliant on him to provide impetus from the middle with Youri Tielemans now in tow and Mainoo beginning the season excellently.
The flip side to that is he’s averaging 5.0 shots per 90 in the league, up from 2.5 in 2025-26; it’s early days of course, but potentially a sign of things to come with him being more of a goal threat. After all, he has already scored four times in all competitions.
Admittedly, his only Premier League goal involvements this season came against Ipswich, when he scored a hat-trick and got an assist, but we all know Fernandes can hurt any opposition.
Can City Nullify United’s Threat in Behind?
If there’s one particular aspect of United’s makeup that City will be conscious of, it’s the threat they pose in behind.
Whether United start Benjamin Sesko or Matheus Cunha up top, Cunha or Marcus Rashford out wide, their attack will be stacked with players who can pose a danger with runs in behind the defence.
That may be even more pertinent against a City side who can leave space behind their defence. On average, they begin their passing sequences 44.2 metres from their own goal – only two teams start higher than that – and they’re the team who’ve spent the smallest proportion of time in a low block this term (9%).
![Premier League low blocks 2026-27](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/premier-league-low-blocks-2026-27-1024x768.jpeg)
United, on the other hand, are second only to Brighton (156) for runs in behind (142). As a proportion of all in-possession runs, United rank top in the Premier League (33.0%).
Bryan Mbeumo is their most active player in this regard. In fact, his 49 runs in behind is more than any other player in the Premier League this season.
![Bryan Mbeumo runs in behind 2026-27](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/bryan-mbeumo-runs-in-behind-2026-27-1024x768.jpeg)
City will presumably adapt slightly to accommodate for United’s biggest threats, but at the same time they’re unlikely to completely change their system and mentality as they’ll be confident of dictating the game as normal.
United should have some opportunities to play to their strengths, then. They’ll need to pick their moments wisely, though, otherwise they may fall into the same offside traps as Porto.
Will City Focus Attacks Down United’s Left?
Manchester United have conceded two goals in each of their three Premier League games this season; while you probably wouldn’t look at any area of their starting XI as being completely terrible, they do have weaknesses.
They have looked particularly susceptible on their left side.
Luke Shaw had an excellent 2025-26 season, playing in every single one of United’s Premier League matches – that was a very surprising feat given his prior injury issues.
But he’s not had a particularly strong start to 2026-27.
He was left for dead by Abdul Fatawu in the lead-up to Ipswich’s first goal, and then against Everton last weekend, he tucked in far too narrowly and was way too slow closing down Tyrique George for the winger’s strike to make it 1-1 at Hill Dickinson Stadium.
![Man Utd attacking third against](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/man-utd-attacking-third-against-1024x768.jpeg)
Of the four non-set-piece goals United have conceded in the Premier League, half have come down Shaw’s side – City may well focus their attention on attacking down that flank. After all, they are crossing more frequently in open play (13.7 per game) this season than in any of the previous three campaigns.
It must be pointed out, however, that Shaw has looked pretty lively going forward, perhaps due to the return of Marcus Rashford. His 2.9 open-play crosses per 90 this term is the left-back’s best return since 2021-22 (3.0) and massively up on 1.2 last term, while his 1.8 open-play chances created per 90 is higher than ever in the Premier League; his 0.4 in 2025-26 was the lowest of his career.
Shaw was rested for United’s 4-0 Champions League win over Sabah. Patrick Dorgu wasn’t entirely convincing defensively while deputising at left-back; whoever plays there on Sunday could be in for a busy evening.

summary: The upcoming Manchester derby at Old Trafford marks Enzo Maresca's first major top-flight test as Manchester City manager, replacing Pep Guardiola. The match features several crucial subplots, including City's defensive vulnerabilities, the prolific derby record of Erling Haaland, and a key midfield battle between Kobbie Mainoo and Elliot Anderson. Additionally, the tactical influence of creators like Bruno Fernandes and Rayan Cherki, alongside United's threat in behind and City's potential focus on United's left flank, could decide the outcome.
key_points: Enzo Maresca takes charge of Manchester City for his first derby, facing a Manchester United side that ranks top for shots and second for expected goals early in the Premier League season.
Erling Haaland enters the fixture with a strong record against United, having scored eight goals in seven Premier League appearances against them.
Midfielders Kobbie Mainoo and Elliot Anderson face off after impressive starts to the domestic campaign and summer international duties respectively.
Manchester United's significant reliance on runs in behind will test a high-defending Manchester City side.
Manchester United have looked susceptible on their left defensive flank, an area Manchester City could target through increased open-play crossing.

title: Carrick explains Tielemans change amid Man Utd team news hint for Man City
author: Tashan Deniran-Alleyne
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
However, with Benjamin Sesko adding a third prior to the break to leave United in a commanding position, Tielemans did not reappear for the second half as he was replaced by Mason Mount.
Meanwhile, Mainoo made way for Andrey Santos just after the hour mark.
“It's nice as well to be able to get Andrey [Santos] and Mason [Mount] on for the second half,” Carrick said.
The United head coach may have dropped a hint over his team selection for the Manchester derby on Sunday as Marcus Rashford, Diogo Dalot and Harry Maguire were all unused substitutes at Old Trafford.
Luke Shaw, though, is a doubt after being left out of the matchday squad altogether after sustaining a knock in the 2-2 draw away at Everton last weekend.
"We tried to manage him so we will see how he is after this one."
summary: Manchester United substituted Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo during their match, allowing Mason Mount and Andrey Santos to play in the second half. Head coach Carrick managed his squad by leaving Marcus Rashford, Diogo Dalot, and Harry Maguire as unused substitutes ahead of the Manchester derby. Meanwhile, Luke Shaw remains a doubt for Sunday's game after sustaining a knock against Everton.
key_points: Mason Mount replaced Youri Tielemans at halftime.
Andrey Santos came on for Kobbie Mainoo just after the hour mark.
Marcus Rashford, Diogo Dalot, and Harry Maguire were unused substitutes.
Luke Shaw is a doubt for the Manchester derby after sustaining a knock against Everton.

title: US Open 2026 results: Elena Rybakina beats Coco Gauff to set up Aryna Sabalenka final
author: Emily Salley; Sam Drury
content:
![Elena Rybakina waves to the crowd](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/1a29/live/8b846990-ad91-11f1-bee3-b1eaca1dd464.jpg)
Elena Rybakina had previously never advanced past the fourth round at the US Open
- Published
Soon-to-be world number one Elena Rybakina produced a gritty comeback against Coco Gauff to reach the US Open final, in which she will face Aryna Sabalenka in a blockbuster showdown between the tournament's top two seeds.
Rybakina is guaranteed to end Sabalenka's 99-week reign as world number one and will replace the Belarusian at the top when the rankings are updated on Monday.
But the Kazakh second seed could rub more salt in Sabalenka's wounds if she can deny the top seed a third successive US Open title in Saturday's showpiece.
Sabalenka sent a warning to her rivals as she overpowered home hope Jessica Pegula 7-5 6-2 to keep alive her bid to become the third woman in the Open era to win the New York singles title three times in a row.
Rybakina will stand in her way after she fought back to beat American fourth seed Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4 and silence the partisan crowd.
"I took a deep breath and just told myself I needed to fight and show good tennis," Rybakina said.
The 27-year-old is chasing her third Grand Slam title after winning Wimbledon in 2022 and beating Sabalenka in January's Australian Open final.
It will be the first time the top two women's seeds have contested a US Open final since Serena Williams beat Victoria Azarenka in the 2013 showpiece.
'I was super desperate' - Sabalenka's 'best match this year'
![Aryna Sabalenka celebrates win against Jessica Pegula to reach US Open final](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/4216/live/cfaac780-ad79-11f1-a78f-b115e8770e5e.jpg)
Aryna Sabalenka is the first player - male or female - to reach eight successive hard-court Grand Slam finals
Sabalenka has not been beaten in New York since losing the 2023 final to Gauff, but there were doubts over her title defence following a poor run-up to the tournament.
After a strong start to the season and winning the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami in March, Sabalenka suffered a quarter-final defeat at Roland Garros and a fourth-round exit at Wimbledon.
However, she has found her form again, dropping just one set en route to the final.
"I was super desperate," Sabalenka said after her win over Pegula.
"It feels for me, talking about Grand Slams, like a last push of the season.
"I wanted it badly to go to the finals, and of course, I want to go all the way."
In a tense opening set, Sabalenka bristled with frustration early on as unforced errors crept into her game while Pegula settled quickly and struck the ball cleanly.
But eventually the four-time major singles winner found her rhythm and, after striking decisively at 6-5 to take the first set, she cranked up the power.
Pegula looked helpless as Sabalenka raced through the second set, with the Belarusian pounding 29 winners to her 12.
The victory meant Sabalenka broke the Open era record for the most Grand Slam hard-court finals in a row, with the 28-year-old reaching every major final on her favoured surface since the 2023 Australian Open.
For 32-year-old Pegula - the only semi-finalist without a Grand Slam title - it is yet another US Open defeat by long-time rival Sabalenka.
Sabalenka denied the third seed a maiden major in the 2024 final, while she also got the better of her in last year's semi-finals - although Pegula had won their most recent meeting in June's Berlin Open.
"I do think she probably would have beaten 99% of people," Pegula said.
"Probably the best match she's played this year."
Rybakina earns chance to back up new number one status
Rybakina's ascent to the top of the world rankings is already assured but she has made it clear that for all the prestige of being number one, winning titles is what she really cares about.
"It's just a number right now, my goal is to win the tournaments which I play," the 27-year-old said before her semi-final.
A three-set victory over Gauff showed all of Rybakina's resilience and ability to absorb a setback - coming from a set down and then being broken when serving for the match - before striking back.
But for much of the match, she was well short of her destructive best.
"I definitely need to step my game up [in the final], serve better than today, stay aggressive and really go for my shots," the two-time major winner added.
The prospect of a final between the top two seeds is tantalising enough but that it is the outgoing number one taking on her successor makes it all the more mouth-watering.
While Sabalenka holds the edge in the head-to-head with 10 wins in 17 meetings, including beating Rybakina in the semi-finals in Miami and the final at Indian Wells this year, the Kazakh came out on top when they met in January's Australian Open final.
Sabalenka led 3-0 in the deciding set in Melbourne but eventually fell to a third defeat in her past four Grand Slam finals.
Meanwhile, Rybakina's only loss in three previous major finals was to Sabalenka in Australia in 2023.
summary: Elena Rybakina overcame a set deficit against Coco Gauff to reach the US Open final, securing her upcoming spot as the world number one. She will face Aryna Sabalenka in the final after Sabalenka defeated Jessica Pegula in straight sets. This marks the first time the top two women's seeds have contested a US Open final since 2013.
key_points: Elena Rybakina beat Coco Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4 to reach her first US Open final.
Rybakina is guaranteed to replace Aryna Sabalenka as the world number one in the updated rankings.
Aryna Sabalenka defeated Jessica Pegula 7-5 6-2 to keep alive her bid for a third consecutive US Open title.
Sabalenka broke the Open era record for reaching eight successive hard-court Grand Slam finals.
The final will feature the tournament's top two seeds in a rematch of January's Australian Open final.

title: Man Utd 4-0 Sabah: Winning return to Champions League as Benjamin Sesko scores again for Michael Carrick's side
author: Adam Bate
content:
Man Utd 4-0 Sabah: Winning return to Champions League as Benjamin Sesko scores again for Michael Carrick's side
Report as Man Utd beat Sabah FC 4-0 at Old Trafford in the Champions League; first-half goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko took the game away from their opponents before Lisandro Martinez made it four after the break
Thursday 10 September 2026 23:16, UK
Manchester United made a winning return to the Champions League as they beat Sabah FC in style with a 4-0 victory at Old Trafford.
The Azerbaijani side started brightly but Matheus Cunha converted Patrick Dorgu's 27th-minute cross and, although Joy-Lance Mickels should have levelled, two goals late in the first half from Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko put United in total control.
Michael Carrick made changes in the second half with the points secure but there was still time for Lisandro Martinez to smash home from close range after some flashy play from Joshua Zirkzee, who produced an eye-catching cameo. Signs of that United swagger.
With goal difference a potentially significant factor in the league phase of this Champions League format, this was a fine night's work on their return. It is Atletico Madrid away next in Europe but there are bigger matters to attend to before that.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Champions League fixtures and results
- Latest news and rumours: Man Utd
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Analysis: Carrick has options
It is over 1000 days since United competed in a Champions League game but this, their 300th in Europe's premier club competition, was not too taxing for Carrick's men. It will be tougher against rivals Manchester City on Sunday - but so will his team selection.
Some of the calls are obvious. Fernandes starred again and the sight of him combining with the equally intelligent Youri Tielemans for United's second was encouraging. The Belgian produced perhaps his best 45 minutes at Old Trafford. But others pressed their case too.
Sesko scored after coming off the bench against Everton and looked sharp here in his first start of the season. With Marcus Rashford also available, and Cunha getting a confidence-boosting goal, there are some interesting decisions ahead for the United boss.
Dorgu enjoyed himself at left-back with Luke Shaw missing from the squad but he was able to play as a de facto winger given United's superiority. It will be more challenging against City's attack but Carrick and his players go into that with confidence restored.
The key moments from Old Trafford
27 - GOAL! Cunha converts Dorgu's cross at the near post
36 - SITTER! Mickels nods wide from inside the six-yard box
42 - GOAL! Fernandes makes it two from Tielemans' pass
45 - GOAL! Mbeumo puts Sesko in to round the goalkeeper
68 - GOAL! Zirkzee's backheel finds Martinez who smashes it in
Carrick: Really encouraging
Man Utd boss Michael Carrick speaking in the press conference:
"I think it was kind of what we set out to achieve, good performance, individually and collectively throughout the game, the boys that started, the boys that came on pitch, clean sheet, goals, exciting football. A good night all round.
"Results-wise, it has not been the start that what we wanted. We wanted more points in the league. But performance-wise, it has been a lot of things we are looking for.
"Collectively, as a team, we have done a lot of the right things and that is why were are excited about what the season will bring. It is really encouraging for me."
On the performance of Benjamin Sesko…
"He definitely offers a different kind of threat, that is the beauty of it really, we know what Ben gives us and there are not many who can give us what he gives us. Speed, physicality, ability to play on the last line and run in behind. Great to have him back."
Dambrauskas: Almost impossible to stop
Sabah head coach Valdas Dambrauskas speaking in the press conference:
"I didn't feel like we were shaking or scared, we tried to play, for the whole 90 minutes we did that. We were escaping from time to time from United pressure.
"We will all go home thinking we could have done better, especially the result. The result could have been a little bit smaller.
"We did not have enough courage probably from the back line to get up. Our centre-backs stayed too deep, not afraid but maybe from inexperience we were over-evaluating the opponent.
"Because when you don't squeeze that space and you allow those players to turn and run it is almost impossible to stop them."
summary: Manchester United made a successful return to the Champions League with a 4-0 victory over Sabah FC at Old Trafford. First-half goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, and Benjamin Sesko established firm control before Lisandro Martinez added a fourth after the break. The win provides Michael Carrick's side with a confidence boost ahead of their upcoming match against Manchester City.
key_points: Matheus Cunha opened the scoring in the 27th minute by converting a cross from Patrick Dorgu.
Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko scored late in the first half to give Manchester United a comfortable lead.
Lisandro Martinez sealed the 4-0 victory in the second half following a setup by Joshua Zirkzee.
The match marked Manchester United's return to the Champions League after over 1,000 days.

title: Manchester United 4-0 Sabah: Champions League – as it happened
author: Daniel Harris
content:
I don’t expect Carrick to make many, if any changes to the team that started against Everton for the City game. He may have considered bolstering midfield with Santos, but Tielemans’ removal at half-time told us that’s not happening. Otherwise, there’s not a chance he puts Yoro up against Haaland, so the only question really concerns the front three. I’d go with Sesko, Mbeumo on the right and Cunha on the left, but I’d be surprised to see that.
Sesko and Dorgu are both happy with the performance and result, with a goal and an assist respectively. Dorgu notes that they’ve conceded too many goals, so the clean sheet is good for the confidence prior to the derby.
That was a decent run-out for United. They’re good in midfield while still improving, and there are goals in their attack, but their defence is still far too easy to get at. It’ll be much harder against City at the weekend, as it will be when they travel to Atletico in their next Champions League game.
A win and a clean sheet for United, who’ll be satisfied – though not, as TNT tell us, Michael Carrick’s first Champions League victory, having taken charge of a game against Villarreal after Ole Gunnar Solaskjaer was sacked.
90+1 min Sabah haven’t given up, Lepinjica finding Mickels with a lovely trivela pass, and the eventuating cross is just as good, picking out Mbina, who leaps well … and thunks a header over the bar.
88 min United couldn’t really win tonight: win comfortably and they were meant to, do anything but and it’s a crisis. But they’ve managed the game fairly well, staying patient, keeping a clean sheet, and given the stage of development they’re at, another 90 is another step towards getting good.
86 min Mickels runs in behind and Lepinjica finds him, down the inside-left channel, away from Mazraoui. He lets fly, but his left-footer swings out and just past the far post.
Almost a consolation for Joy-Lance Mickels. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images
83 min Lacey has really nice feet and isn’t shy at all, but I wonder if he’ll be physical enough for the Prem. I’m not sure he’s got the p&p to go on the outside, so perhaps he’s a 10 not a winger, but will he be able to contribute enough in midfield to play there? He’s got proper technical ability, though, so should have a decent career in the game.
81 min “The second half of Slavia Praha v Racing Club de Lens has been eventfl,” says Kári Tulinius. “In the 49th minute Mikulas Konecny was sent off, and he’d only come on as a substitute at half time. Nevertheless Danijel Šturm gave the home side the lead just two minutes later. They were making a good fist of holding on until Abdullah Sima equalised for the French side. The final bit of the match promises more drama.”
77 min United work well through midfield, Santos and Mount to the fore; there’s a decent chance they start together against Brighton in the League Cup next week, and I really like the way they combine. From having next to no midfield, such that Amorim put Bruno in it because he felt he had no choice – he did, he had Mainoo – they now have quality and options.
75 min Naturally, the corner comes to nothing. I’m not sure why, when sesko was on, United weren’t looking for him, either for near-post flick-ons or to go for goal.
74 min Zirkzee is a kind of diet Berbatov, and he shows lovely feet to wriggle between two challenges before chopping outside, narrowing his own shooting angle, and when the left-footed effort comes, it’s blocked behind for a corner.
Fernandes flips over the wall and Zirkzee, right of centre and facing the touchline, backheels. The ball then ricochets off McCarthy, Dashdamirov and Pokatilov, before Martinez slams into the net from close range. the keeper and defenders won’t mind never, ever seeing that again.
Lisandro Martinez makes it four! Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images
Matheus Cunha points to an unlikely scorer. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA
66 min “Bodo’s final third is toothless right where the game is decided - the final 16 metres,” advises AnhTuan Nguyen Huynh. They now trail Bayern 2-0, Musiala and Kane with the goals. Except Kane’s may be chalked off for this infraction against all laws of decency.
6o min United are back dominating possession, probing as they seek a fourth goal … and they almost get one, working it patiently and well before Bruno, back to goal, allows the ball to slide down the outside of his foot for Cunha, whose low shot is saves by a sprawling Pokatilov.
58 min Mount swishes a cunning pass through the lines for Mbeumo, who finds Mazraoui and takes a man away with a run outside him. So the full-back cuts inside, tries a curler for the far top corner … and gets naewhere near it
55 min United are sitting off Sabah now, conserving energy. I’m a little surprised Mainoo wasn’t withdrawn, as he’s essential to all they’re trying to do, but I doubt he completes the 90.
summary: Manchester United secured a 4-0 victory and a clean sheet against Sabah, providing a confidence boost ahead of their upcoming fixtures. Players like Sesko and Dorgu contributed with a goal and an assist respectively, while the team showcased improvements in midfield and attack. However, observers noted that United's defense still remains vulnerable as tougher challenges loom against City and Atletico.
key_points: Manchester United defeated Sabah 4-0 with goals including a late strike from Lisandro Martinez.
Both Sesko and Dorgu expressed satisfaction with the performance, highlighting the value of keeping a clean sheet.
The team displayed strong options in midfield with players like Santos and Mount performing well.
Despite the comfortable win, analysts pointed out that United's defense still looks too easy to breach ahead of tougher matches.

title: England vs Pakistan: Ollie Robinson strikes twice in first over of second innings as hosts dominate day two of third Test at Edgbaston
author: David Currie
content:
England vs Pakistan: Ollie Robinson strikes twice in first over of second innings as hosts dominate day two of third Test at Edgbaston
Ollie Robinson dismissed Saim Ayub for a pair and Abdullah Shafique in first over of Pakistan second innings; England seamer has 28 wickets in four Tests this summer, at an average of 7.75 apiece; watch day three live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am, Friday
Thursday 10 September 2026 19:21, UK
England are closing in on the most emphatic of series sweeps of Pakistan after reducing the visitors to 52-2 - still 268 runs behind - before rain ended play early on day two of the third Test at Edgbaston.
Pakistan's score at stumps actually represented somewhat of a recovery after their prospects looked even gloomier than the darkening skies overhead when reduced to 0-2 in Ollie Robinson's first over.
Robinson (2-10) saw off Saim Ayub first ball - the opener, one of four players flown straight into the team after seven were axed from the touring squad, out for a pair - before Abdullah Shafique also nicked to the slips three deliveries later.
It means that Robinson now has 28 wickets across his four Test appearances this summer, taking them at a staggering 7.75 apiece. In this series that improves even further to 6.66.
Joe Root's grab at slip to send back Shafique moved him one clear of Australia's Steve Smith and onto 220 in their personal battle to claim the most catches by an outfielder in Test cricket.
The clatter of wickets didn't follow as it had in Pakistan's first innings, with Azan Awais (29no) and Shan Masood (21no) sharing a fifty stand before the rain arrived - albeit Masood was put down on 13 by Ben Duckett, his third spill of the Test, off the unfortunate Gus Atkinson.
Brook, Lawrence and Smith all miss out with Test tons looming
Earlier, England were bowled out for 452, earning a 320-run lead on first innings as Dan Lawrence (65), Jamie Smith (69) and Robinson (50) added half-centuries to those notched by Emilio Gay (60) and Harry Brook (75) on day one.
Brook added 23 to his overnight total before he was the first wicket to fall on the second morning, just at the point where he and Dan Lawrence - who had stormed through to a 47-ball fifty - had seemingly broken Pakistan's spirits with 73 scored off the opening 10 overs of the day.
The breakthrough was a gift, Brook practically running himself out as he called for a risky single to midwicket, where Masood did the honours with a direct hit.
The scoring didn't slow as Smith joined Lawrence at the crease, the pair putting on 64 together before Lawrence was left kicking himself as he chopped one from Mohammad Imran (2-47) back onto his stumps just before lunch.
Smith was the next through to fifty - off 54 balls - but failed to convert as, after Gus Atkinson (19) was bowled by a beauty from Imran, Smith chipped one back to the fired-up Razaullah (4-148).
While he was okay to bat, Smith would later be absent from the field - Jordan Cox subbing in at wicketkeeper - with the regular gloveman nursing an injured finger from the first day.
Robinson, hitting a second Test half-century, and Jofra Archer (32no) had some fun lower down the order, finding the boundary - or clearing it - with regularity as England pushed their total above 400 and lead beyond 300 before the innings was finally ended.
Pakistan carried their increasingly timid approach in the field over into the start of their second innings, and a two-day finish briefly looked a possibility after Robinson's double strike in the first over, before Azan and Masood showed some much-needed resilience and the rain intervened.
Lawrence 'gutted' to miss out on century
Lawrence was "gutted" at blowing the prospect of a first international century.
The 29-year-old, who made 51 at Headingley and 54 at Lord's in this series, said: "I'm obviously gutted that I didn't kick on and make a really big score, but I was pretty happy with how I did overall.
"I felt like I was playing really nicely and it was a really good surface to bat on against the tiring attack. I thought I was going to make a really big score to be honest, but it wasn't meant to be.
"I've missed out on two chances to make really big scores and really big contributions - at Headingley and here.
"But I'm quite happy with how I've played. I've got three fifties in four innings (in this series), which is pretty good. I think if I was offered 65 at the start of the day, I'd have taken it."
Meanwhile, seamer Robinson has been the star of the series with 21 wickets at a preposterous average of 6.66 - when he dismissed Shafique for the fifth time in six innings, it was 6.19 - and Lawrence, one of England's slip fielders, admitted the cordon have to be on red alert when the seamer is bowling.
Lawrence added: "When he's bowling, when he's putting it in the same spot pretty much every ball, you always feel in the game.
"The wickets have offered quite a lot to us as well and all the seamers. You certainly do feel in the game behind the stumps, especially when you've got someone pretty much at the peak of his powers."
Nasser: Ayub shouldn't be here
Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain:
"Saim Ayub, in particular, struggled. The truth is he shouldn't be here. He came from the CPL [Caribbean Premier League] and hasn't played first-class cricket in 11 months.
"I don't know who thinks it's the right thing to fly someone over from foreign conditions, and think they'll be fine in these conditions against a Duke's ball and Ollie Robinson's bowling attack? It's showing disrespect to Test match cricket.
"The players who are here, their friends and room-mates have been axed. People who have got five-fors have been axed.
"How you treat players is so important. It's a two-way thing when players are presented with a Test cap. You're expected to meet the core values of representing Pakistan, but the team needs to look after the players in return.
"That goes the moment you send seven people home. People start looking after themselves. Why should I bother about a team that doesn't bother about me and has sent my team-mates home between Tests?
"This Pakistan side, not only are they in poor form, they look like a team that says, 'what will be, will be', and just looks after itself."

summary: England dominated day two of the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston, building a 320-run first-innings lead after being bowled out for 452. Seamer Ollie Robinson then claimed two wickets in the first over of Pakistan's second innings. Rain eventually ended play early with Pakistan struggling at 52-2, still 268 runs behind.
key_points: England posted 452 in their first innings, backed by half-centuries from Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith, and Ollie Robinson.
Ollie Robinson dismissed Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique in the first over of Pakistan's second innings, leaving the visitors at 0-2.
Azan Awais and Shan Masood shared an unbeaten fifty-stand before rain brought an early end to day two with Pakistan at 52-2.
Joe Root surpassed Steve Smith to claim 220 catches, the most by an outfielder in Test cricket.

The Premier League has announced it will stage seven matches on Boxing Day this year after releasing its festive schedule.
Four fixtures will be staged at 15:00 GMT, with further matches played at 12:30, 17:30 and 20:00.
The fixture programme for 26 December, which falls on a Saturday in 2026, is considerably bigger than last year, when one game was held.
Three matches will be played on Sunday, 27 December, while three further rounds of games will be held over a period up to Thursday, 7 January.
A round of evening midweek fixtures will staged on 29-30 December, while Leeds will host Everton (20:00) for the only match on New Year's Day.
The remainder of that round will be held over the weekend of 2-3 January, with the fourth round of games spread across the evenings of 5-7 January.
The Premier League has brought forward the announcement of fixture scheduling over the Christmas and New Year period after consultation with both broadcast partners and the Football Supporters' Association and representatives from club Fan Advisory Boards.
Television scheduling for Premier League fixtures has been announced up to Monday, 2 November, with broadcast selections for the remaining games in November and December to be announced in the weeks commencing 21 September and 19 October respectively.
The Premier League has guaranteed clubs at least a 60-hour break between fixtures over the festive period to address the concerns over a congested festive schedule that follows recent expansions of the European and international calendars.

title: Arsenal: Martin Odegaard new role explained by Mikel Arteta after captain's Champions League winner at Napoli
author: Peter Smith; Nick Wright
content:
Arsenal: Martin Odegaard new role explained by Mikel Arteta after captain's Champions League winner at Napoli
Martin Odegaard scored his fourth goal in five games this season with the winner in Arsenal's 1-0 Champions League victory at Napoli on Wednesday; Gunners captain only scored once in 2025/26 but higher position and fitness have facilitated fast start to the new campaign
Thursday 10 September 2026 07:18, UK
Martin Odegaard is a player transformed at the start of this season - and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta puts his captain's impressive form down to fitness and new positioning.
Odegaard was the match-winner again for Arsenal on Wednesday, thumping in the only goal of the game in the Champions League victory at Napoli.
That hit followed his clinching strike against Chelsea in the Premier League on Sunday and takes his total to four goals in five appearances this season across all competitions.
Odegaard only scored once for Arsenal during an injury-hit 2025/26 campaign but now his stats are up across a range of other attacking metrics, too.
- Napoli 0-1 Arsenal - Match report and analysis
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Champions League scores
- Latest news and rumours: Arsenal
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
"First of all he needs to be available and last year he missed so many games through injuries," said Arteta when asked in his post-match press conference about Odegaard's improvement.
"The quality's always been there. It's never been a question," added Declan Rice, speaking to Sky Sports. "Last year, to have two shoulder injuries like he did, then a MCL injury he did, it's never easy.
"But then you see him at the World Cup and how he's started this year. That's the Martin we know and we love, he's our captain. We need to keep giving him the ball and letting things happen."
Arteta also highlighted how fresh combinations with team-mates are playing a part.
"He's got that edge and different relationships around him as well and that helps," said the Gunners boss.
"He can start to go by different heights in the team, especially in the attacking phase, and when we get him into those positions he's a really dangerous player."
That is demonstrated by Odegaard's touches in the opposition box going up from 2.5 per 90 minutes last season to 4.3 per 90 minutes so far this term.
Arteta put Odegaard's freedom to advance into more threatening positions down to the skills of his team-mates in open play, which the Arsenal head coach suggested had been missing previously.
"We have a lot of players that can take the ball there and progress the ball much better than we did in the past," Arteta explained.
"When that happens, [Odegaard] needs to take different heights and angles and positions in order to disorganise the opponent and he's done that really well."
Christos Tzolis is likely to be one of those players Arteta is referencing. The summer signing has four assists to his name already, with three of those coming for Odegaard goals, including the winner in Naples.
But the Arsenal attack down both flanks and through the middle looked extremely dangerous at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
Arsenal had 26 shots in total - their most on record (since 2003/04) in the competition. An expected goals total of 4.05 showed they should have got far more for their efforts.
Odegaard, though, did step up and deliver the key moment.
"That's what we need," said Arteta. "The players with the mindset to decide a game and play with personality. To keep taking chances and risks.
"He's getting into those positions much more in recent games and now you feel he has the emotional state that he knows the ball can go in, and he scored an incredible goal tonight."
Odegaard playing with freedom and flair
Analysis by Sky Sports' Nick Wright:
Odegaard is a player in form. That much was clear from early in the game against Napoli. He oozed class and confidence, demanding the ball then finding the gaps in Napoli's defence and threading passes forward. Everything went through him.
His goal, brilliantly taken from the edge of the box after a 29-pass build-up, proved crucial. He now has four in five games this season, a stunning turnaround having only managed one in 36 last term. Odegaard, uninhibited by injuries, looks a different player.
Showing his team-mates how to finish was only one part of his performance. He also ended the game having had more touches, made more passes and created more chances than anyone else on the pitch. Napoli couldn't really get near him.
The scooped pass to release Ben White for the golden chance somehow spurned by Piero Hincapie was one of many examples of his ingenuity against the massed ranks of Napoli players but there were plenty of others. He played with freedom and flair.
"Martin is contributing goals," added Arteta after the game. "That is obviously impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players, to be decisive, and certainly he was that today."
Arsenal continue to feel the benefits.
summary: Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard scored the winning goal in a 1-0 Champions League victory against Napoli, bringing his total to four goals in five appearances this season. Manager Mikel Arteta attributes Odegaard's impressive early-season form to improved fitness following an injury-plagued previous campaign, alongside a new higher attacking position. Teammate Declan Rice and fresh squad combinations have also helped facilitate the midfielder's fast start.
key_points: Martin Odegaard scored the winner in Arsenal's 1-0 Champions League victory against Napoli.
Odegaard has recorded four goals in five appearances this season after scoring only once during an injury-hit 2025/26 campaign.
Mikel Arteta explained that improved fitness and a higher attacking position have driven Odegaard's strong form.
Odegaard's touches in the opposition box have increased from 2.5 per 90 minutes last season to 4.3 per 90 minutes this term.
Summer signing Christos Tzolis has contributed significantly by providing three assists for Odegaard goals.

title: Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid: Alexis Mac Allister scores stunning winner as Bradley Barcola has eventful full debut
author: Adam Bate
content:
Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid: Alexis Mac Allister scores stunning winner as Bradley Barcola has eventful full debut
Report as Andoni Iraola’s Champions League career as a coach begins with a 2-1 Liverpool win over Atletico Madrid thanks to Alexis Mac Allister's strike; Dominik Szoboszlai levelled Marcos Llorente’s goal; Bradley Barcola off with "cramp" on full debut
Wednesday 9 September 2026 22:49, UK
Alexis Mac Allister's superb strike saw Liverpool come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 at Anfield as Bradley Barcola went off with "cramp" on an eventful home debut.
Barcola was making his first start for Liverpool but felt his calf in the second half and the £123m signing was substituted having missed three good chances to mark the occasion with a goal. It did not impact the result thanks to Mac Allister's rocket.
Marcos Llorente had opened the scoring for the Spanish side with his fifth goal against Liverpool when put through well by Julian Alvarez on the Argentine forward's return to the starting line-up. But that man Dominik Szoboszlai levelled it up before the break.

Curiously, both Liverpool goals came in the immediate aftermath of Barcola chances. Jan Oblak saved to deny him in the build-up to Szoboszlai's goal, Ronald Araujo cleverly recycling the chance. And Mac Allister blasted in to spare his blushes for the second.
Liverpool had drawn their first two Premier League games of the season two apiece, and given the open nature of the game there was a risk of a repeat. But instead Andoni Iraola earned this Anfield victory in his first Champions League match as a head coach.
The key moments from Anfield
1 - CHANCE! Szoboszlai robs Koke but Isak drags his shot wide
15 - SAVE! Barcola chance in behind on the right but Oblak saves
17 - GOAL! Alvarez sends Llorente through and he beats Alisson
27 - SAVE! Alvarez shot from distance tipped just wide by Alisson
30 - SAVE! Wirtz denied by Oblak after starting the move himself
40 - GOAL! Araujo's clever flick puts Szoboszlai in to slot home
49 - WIDE! Wirtz sends Barcola clean through but he shoots wide
50 - GOAL! Mac Allister blasts in left-footed just second later
58 - INJURY! Barcola substituted after going down holding his calf
88 - OFFSIDE! Frimpong sweeps the ball home but is well offside
Iraola: Just cramp for Barcola
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola speaking about Bradley Barcola in the press conference:
"No, it's cramp. It's just cramp, there is no injury. With Bradley, it's about building his physical condition.
"We don't really know, or we didn't know until now probably, how much he can play, because he hasn't had any minutes in pre-season for PSG.
"He played 30 the other day. Today we had some question marks, how many minutes he can give us, and probably now we know.
"And I'm very happy because also he has had two very clear chances against the keeper. He hasn't scored, but I want him there. That is where he has to make the difference - arriving to those spots, those positions.
"And I'm very happy because in, I don't know how many minutes he's played, two times against the keeper is a good sign with Bradley."
Analysis: Barcola's Anfield debut
Sky Sports' Adam Bate at Anfield:
Barcola might have scored twice in the first half on his Anfield bow and missed a big chance at the start of the second but it was still a promising performance. He has been used on the left by Paris Saint-Germain but showed his versatility playing from the right.
His fitness looked sharper than his finishing and it did not take long for him to win over the Kop, his name being chanted inside 15 minutes when he tracked back to shut down an early Atletico counter-attack. That pace looks like it will be a real weapon for Iraola.
The worry was the sight of him trudging off before the hour. The Liverpool boss had stressed the need to manage Barcola given that he had not been involved in pre-season. Iraola needs him up to speed quickly. On this evidence, he can make a difference.
summary: Liverpool secured a 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid in the Champions League thanks to a stunning winning strike from Alexis Mac Allister. Marcos Llorente initially opened the scoring for Atletico before Dominik Szoboszlai equalized before halftime. Bradley Barcola experienced an eventful full debut for Liverpool, missing several scoring chances before being substituted with cramp in the second half.
key_points: Alexis Mac Allister scored the winning goal with a powerful left-footed strike.
Marcos Llorente opened the scoring for Atletico Madrid, assisted by Julian Alvarez.
Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool's first-half equalizer.
Bradley Barcola made his full debut for Liverpool, missed three scoring chances, and was substituted in the second half with cramp.
The win marked Andoni Iraola's first Champions League victory as a head coach.

title: Ødegaard ‘edge’ delights Arteta as Arsenal secure narrow win at Napoli
author: Ed Aarons
content:
After their record-breaking feats last year in the Champions League, Arsenal are at it again. But having been delayed along with hundreds of travelling supporters by travel chaos on Tuesday, Mikel Arteta’s side had to bide their time against Napoli until Martin Ødegaard continued his rich vein of goalscoring with the crucial strike 15 minutes from full time.
Perhaps it was the fact that, at Uefa’s insistence, they were forced to wear red shorts for the first time since a Premier League game against Watford in 2022 that Arsenal were not quite at their flowing best here and missed a hatful of chances.
Yet they were deserved winners in the end and the substitute Noni Madueke should have made the victory more comprehensive late on.
Having come so close to breaking their duck in this competition last year after becoming the first team to win all eight of their league stage matches, Arsenal look capable of going one better this time if Ødegaard can keep up this sparkling form.
He now has four goals in his last five games after scoring once in all competitions last year and it was the Norway captain whose name was being chanted by the fans who were kept behind more than an hour after the final whistle.
“That’s what we need – players with that mindset to decide the game and to play with that personality,” said Arteta. “He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games and I feel he has this emotional state that he knows that the ball can go in. He’s got that edge and he’s now got different relationships around him [in the team] as well. That helps.”
Arteta has bad memories of this stadium after being sent off in a 2-0 defeat during the Champions League group stage in 2013. But Arsenal’s most recent match here ended in victory as they qualified for the Europa League semi-finals under Unai Emery in 2019. Both clubs have been crowned domestic champions since then, with Napoli ending their 33-year wait in 2023 then doing it again two years later. Yet Champions League success has continued to elude them after finishing 30th in the league phase last season.
![Mikel Arteta talks with Kevin De Bruyne, the former Manchester City midfielder, after the match](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/480663030665d41e966918f0a7ed9ff1bbb63fc1/0_0_2300_1495/master/2300.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
That was in stark contrast to Arsenal, who were unbeaten over 14 matches before falling at the final hurdle. It was telling that Arteta kept faith with four of his back five that started against Chelsea on Sunday, with Piero Hincapié replacing Riccardo Calafiori at left-back but failing to match the Italian’s finishing ability with one glaring miss. Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyökeres also made their first starts of the season but largely disappointed, with the Sweden striker making way for Kai Havertz just before Ødegaard’s winner.
Those Arsenal supporters that did make it to southern Italy had no problem making themselves heard throughout, with plenty of empty seats in the home sections despite Max Allegri’s attempts to rally Napoli’s fans beforehand. The game quickly settled into a pattern as the visitors set up camp in Napoli’s half and the hosts attempted to hit them on the break. Kevin De Bruyne – no stranger to facing Arsenal after a decade in the sky blue of Manchester City – forced David Raya into a rare mistake after a typically driving run through the midfield but the ball was scrambled away to safety.
That came just after a spectacular overhead kick from Bukayo Saka at the other end had been saved by Alex Meret. Merino should have scored when he was set up by Eze’s clever header across the face of goal before Ben White drilled a shot straight into Meret’s grateful gloves.
after newsletter promotion
Matteo Politano managed to test Raya again as Napoli continued to find gaps in Arsenal’s normally watertight defence. Saka blazed over after a brilliant through ball from Ødegaard on the stroke of half-time, with replays confirming the assistant had been wrong to raise his flag.
![Martin Ødegaard scores the only goal of the match at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/708e7b03bd110881956f0dd4f0118917465a5fa0/919_128_3110_2488/master/3110.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Meret did not return for the second half and was replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, once on Manchester United’s books. The Serbia goalkeeper was a mere spectator for a flowing Arsenal move featuring a sumptuous scooped pass into the area that ended with Hincapié missing the target after being picked out at the far post by Ben White’s header. Suddenly Napoli found themselves suffocated by a blanket of red. Allegri, who knows what it feels like to have lost in a Champions League final after suffering that fate twice in three years at Juventus, responded by switching to a back five and trying to hang on.
Arsenal’s pressure eventually told when another substitute, Christos Tzolis, exchanged passes with White and teed up Ødegaard, whose shot flew in off the post despite Milinkovic-Savic just getting his fingertips to the ball. Havertz had a goal disallowed for offside in injury time, but the mission was already complete.
summary: Arsenal secured a narrow victory away at Napoli after overcoming pre-match travel chaos. Despite missing numerous chances, Martin Ødegaard scored the crucial winning goal 15 minutes before full time. The victory continues Arsenal's strong form in the Champions League under manager Mikel Arteta.
key_points: Martin Ødegaard scored the only goal of the match 15 minutes from time.
Arsenal missed several scoring chances before breaking the deadlock.
Manager Mikel Arteta praised Ødegaard's decisive mindset and recent goalscoring form.
The victory keeps Arsenal on a strong trajectory in the Champions League.

title: Chelsea 6-3 Leeds; Liverpool 2-1 Atlético Madrid, PSG 6-1 Slovan Bratislava – live
author: Daniel Harris
content:
Iraola is chatting to TNT, saying he loved the occasion and that he takes some responsibility for the first-half performance, having not predicted Atleti’s 3-5-2; he corrected halfway through the first half.
He’s happy he side showed character, but they’ve difficult homes and nasty aways, so there’s a lot to do. Barcola, he advises, had cramp, an absolute result, and he goes on to say this is a new team without the mechanisms in which every player knows what to do in every situation.
On Araujo, Iraola says he has good crossing ability, is good in the air and smart with his decision-making. Players like Frimpong and Tsimikas have’t played much, so are probably disappointed, but they contributed tonight.
Neto screeches down the right and cuts back to the edge, where Barco shanks horribly, only for Welbeck, always alert, to redirect into the net via header. What a ridiculous half (of football) this has been.
Danny Welbeck (right) heads home for his second, and Chelsea’s sixth, goal of the game. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA
Which he’s pretty happy about. Photograph: Isabel Infantes/Reuters
“Iraolaball has started rolling, slowly but steadily,” reckons Rupak Pramanik. “This Liverpool looked a lot like the Liverpool opponents feared during the Klopp era.”
Generous, I’d say – they were very vulnerable in the first half and the players just aren’t as good as those Klopp had, nor have they the physicality to play at the same tempo. But they played some decent stuff in parts.
Six additional minutes at Stamford Bridge,enough time for Chelsea to score and concede at least another couple. If they can get the defence and midfield right, in January and in the summer, they could be very nasty next season.
Atleti played well in the first half but Liverpool hung in there and were much the better side in the second. That’s a really important win for Andoni Iraoloa, his debut Champions League game and a difficult opponent sorted in uplifting manner.
Rogers has been filth since coming on and this, his third assist, sees him zoom down the left and cross low, the ball eluding all but Barco, on the far side of the box, and he lashes in a low finish. Surely the game is now over.
A corner is half-cleared and, when the ball is tucked back across by Dro, it hits a defender and falls into the path of Ruiz, who donkey-kicks into the net.
Paris St Germain's Fabian Ruiz (right) celebrates scoring their sixth goal. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters
Munoz, on as sub, breaks into the Atleti box and diddles his man by dipping infield, only to shoot too close to Oblak, who palms out Frimpong is there to ram home the rebound, but was offside when the intial shot was taken.
“Couple of Scottish Premier games tonight,” advises Simon McMahon – yes I’ve got them on my vidiprinter. “Rangers scoring in stoppage time to defeat St. Mirren by a goal to nil, while Celtic are leading by the same score at St. Johnstone with five minutes to go. The teams meet in the Scottish League Cup quarter=final on Sunday. Expect handshakes, pats on the back and general bonhomie all round fireworks.”
Grown-men action looks inevitable, even though away fans have been banned.
It’s been a quieter second half at Anfield – well, since the flurry at the start of it, when Liverpool scored their second goal. Atleti were really dangerous in the first, but have been largely shut down – and have, I think, missed Lee, who was hooked.
Incidentally, I love The Prestige, Christopher Nolan’s best film by a mile, in mine – it has blather and keks, which I don’t always find to be the case with him.
“There’s something uncanny about this PSG, as if they’re not fully synced up with reality,” says Kári Tulinius. “I can’t think of many teams that have had me entirely lose track of what’s going on, where the players and the ball just aren’t where they should be. At the risk of spoiling the movie The Prestige, while other sides are working within the parameters of the real, the Parisians seem to have found technology that allows them to break the bounds of physical space.”
They’re kind of the next version of Guardiola’s Barca, every player a technician but not, as you intimate, part of a system that tells them where to be and when; rather, they’re trusted to make sure that somebody is.
It’s a kicking! Rogers flies down the right and cut back along the carpet, Welbeck feinting to leave it for Palmer before taking it back the way it came and lashing low into the net. This is a seriously engaging football tea.
Danny Welbeck celebrates after extending Chelsea’s lead. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images
Arsenal pop it about on the edge, Guimaraes into Tzolis, right of the box, and he plays back out to Odegaard, who laces a belting finish low into the far corner. You wondered if he was taking a step when he started crashing the box at the start of this season, and by the looks of things, that’s exactly what he’s doing.
Arsenal's Martin Odegaard opens the scoring. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters
It’s three goal in seven minutes! Palmer feeds Rogers in the middle, and he slides in to poke Neto, at inside-left. But there’s still a lot of work to do, the body opened and the finish passed low into the far corner. Chelsea aren’t great at the back, but goodness me, they’ve got some useful attackers.
Chelsea's Pedro Neto puts the home side ahead. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA
Neto (left) wheels away in celebration as Stamford Bridge erupts. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters
Spain press conference epa02237461 Spanish National Team player Jesus Navas smiles as he goes to press center on 05 July 2010 a Photograph: Juan Carlos C rdenas/EPA
I wonder what Enzo Maresca and Thomas Tuchel are making of Palmer so far this season. Every serious squad needs a maverick or two, and misunderstanding them says more about the managers than the players.
A throw goes towards Rogers, who kind of shrugs it off to Palmer, on the edge, and, using the defender as a screen to block the keeper’s view, he curves a low finish into the far bottom corner, the goal not unlike the one he scored for England in the Euro final.
All eyes are on the ball as Cole Palmer’s shot heads towards the far corner. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA
summary: This live-updating football report covers multiple matches, highlighting Chelsea's high-scoring win featuring goals from Danny Welbeck, Cole Palmer, and Pedro Neto. Liverpool secured an important Champions League victory against Atlético Madrid following a strong second half. Meanwhile, Paris St Germain recorded a heavy 6-1 win over Slovan Bratislava, and various other domestic and European results unfolded.
key_points: Chelsea secured a high-scoring victory with standout performances and goals from players including Danny Welbeck, Cole Palmer, and Pedro Neto.
Liverpool earned an important Champions League win against Atlético Madrid after overcoming a vulnerable first-half performance.
Paris St Germain defeated Slovan Bratislava with a dominant 6-1 scoreline.
Manager Andoni Iraola praised his side's character after successfully adjusting his tactics following Atlético's initial 3-5-2 setup.

Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid preview
Liverpool beat Atletico Madrid 3-2 on matchday one of the Champions League last season and punters should expect another high-scoring clash at Anfield.
Reds manager Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first Champions League match, five days after claiming his first Premier League win with Liverpool at Ipswich.
His side looked shaky in 2-2 draws with Newcastle and Nottingham Forest but Alexander Isak scored twice in the first ten minutes at Portman Road to set up a welcome 2-0 victory.
While Iraola is a Champions League rookie, his opposite number Diego Simeone has overseen 128 matches in the competition.
Only Carlo Ancelotti, Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola, Arsene Wenger and Jose Mourinho have more Champions League experience than Simeone, who took Atletico to the final in 2014 and 2016.
Last season, they knocked out Barcelona in the quarter-finals and ran Arsenal close in a 2-1 aggregate defeat in the semis.
However, Atletico's campaign also included that opening defeat at Anfield, a 4-0 league-phase mauling by Arsenal and a 3-2 loss to Igor Tudor's Tottenham.
They had beaten Spurs 5-2 in a chaotic last-16 first leg and their defence was exposed again in Saturday's 3-0 La Liga defeat at Athletic Bilbao.
In the early years of Simeone's reign, Atletico were renowned for their defensive steel. More recently, though, they have been a far softer touch, particularly away from home.
Before their gritty semi-final against Arsenal, there were over 2.5 goals in 12 of Atletico's 14 European games last term and one of the exceptions was a 2-0 away win over ten-man Barcelona.
Star striker Julian Alvarez, strongly linked with a summer move to Barca or Arsenal, has made only two substitute appearances and may have to stew on the bench for a little longer.
Lee Kang-In, Ademola Lookman and Alex Baena have been used as forwards in a fluid 4-4-2 formation but Atletico look set for a high-scoring defeat at Anfield.
Liverpool finished top of the Champions League standings in 2024-25 and third last season, despite their poor Premier League campaign under Arne Slot.
Champions Paris Saint-Germain knocked them out in both seasons but Atletico are far less intimidating opponents.
Bradley Barcola, a two-time Champions League winner with PSG, could make his Liverpool debut and the Reds' attackers can ensure a memorable night for Iraola.

He named his dog "Anfield" to celebrate those goalscoring feats but could show too much bite in the tackle for the referee's liking this evening.
Liverpool have a host of dangerous wide players, including new signing Barcola. Llorente picked up nine yellow cards and one red last season and was booked against Sevilla on his first start of the new campaign.
