title: Edd Straw's 2026 Italian Grand Prix F1 driver rankings
author: Edd Straw
content:
The Italian Grand Prix delivered a lot of action and a particularly memorable home win - though the local crowds also had to contend with the home team tripping up badly.
Those two things cover off the two opposite ends of our driver rankings this week, but what about the rest of the field?
Want to quiz Edd on his driver rankings? Sign up to The Race Members' Club to do exactly that - and ask your questions in reply to this post.
Champions-tier members can also try their hand at putting their own driver rankings together for Edd to react to in a separate feature!
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/MERCEDES_KA.png)
Started: 19th Finished: 1st
PROS
- Hinted with his Q2 lap and his out-of-sequence no-tow Q3 lap that he had the pace for pole despite not focusing on single-lap pace through the weekend.
- Incisiveness both on the two opening laps (gaining a total of seven places), then in clearing cars to get to Russell, was key to pulling off his unexpected win.
- Showed no sign of the pressure of either the championship situation or being at Monza, where he'd had tough times both in 2024 and 2025, getting to him.
CONS
- There were circumstances that played in his favour, even though he still had to drive superbly to capitalise on them.
- The error in battle when he was caught out by the breaking-up track surface while attacking Russell late on led to a trip through the gravel that could have been more costly, although he recovered well.
Verdict: The difficulty of his mission means the gravel moment doesn't cost him top spot.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/ALPINE_PG.png)
Started: 1st Finished: 7th
PROS
- His execution of qualifying was close to flawless, finding pace as the session progressed, positioning himself well for tows and putting together his best three sectors on the all-important pole lap.
- Drove intelligently in the race, realising that the race pace of the Alpine was such that he was inevitably going to fall behind the big-team cars. That said, he covered Norris for some time, so he did what he could.
- Realistically, top of the midfield in seventh place was the optimum race result.
CONS
- Nothing of any real note - and in the race that's impressive given his team-mate showed what could go wrong if you got overambitious in an Alpine.
Verdict: Backed up his brilliant qualifying with an intelligent race.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/MERCEDES_GR.png)
Started: 2nd Finished: 2nd
PROS
- Raced intelligently, particularly in the way he forced Antonelli into an error when attempting to hang onto the lead late on.
- Dealt well with the front tyre vibration in the closing stages to minimise the time loss.
- The VSC timing was unfortunate, allowing Antonelli to make a cheap stop and transforming the trajectory of the battle at the front.
CONS
- Should have taken pole position, but a combination of struggling with brake locking and being too close to Max Verstappen on his final Q3 lap contributed to him slipping behind Gasly.
- Appeared to lack Antonelli's edge of pace, although direct comparisons are difficult because of the different approaches to qualifying and race strategy.
Verdict: Better than the narrative that he 'flopped' suggests, but not at Antonelli's level.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/WILLIAMS_CS.png)
Started: 13th Finished: 13th
PROS
- Produced what he called "mini wins" in qualifying by reaching Q2 and beating Esteban Ocon, by 0.001s, and couldn't have qualified higher.
- Made the most of the cheap virtual safety car pitstop to come through to 13th, making the most of that opportunity to finish higher than a Williams should have done.
CONS
- Despite getting a good launch at the start, he was shuffled back by the end of the lap - albeit only behind quicker cars.
Verdict: After big errors in the last two events, was back on car-maximising form.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/RB_AL.png)
Started: 9th Finished: 8th
PROS
- At times, showed impressive pace and appeared to be on top of the car for the most part.
- Eighth was probably the best he could achieve given he never showed the speed to threaten Gasly.
- Drove a good, clean race despite seeming to struggle a little more with ageing hards than Gasly.
CONS
- Q3 was a disappointment, and he apologised over the radio for leaving time on the table - albeit he suggested that was only in the vicinity of a tenth.
- Perhaps over-managed for much of the hard stint, but that was down to instructions from the team so doesn't really count against him.
Verdict: Another Q3 underperformance aside, a good weekend.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/RED-BULL_MV.png)
Started: 5th Finished: 3rd
PROS
- Third place in the grand prix was the best possible result.
- Hung around the lead battle while he could despite the Red Bull not being as quick, which was not easy given the deployment disadvantage to Mercedes.
- When the car was working as it should, he generally extracted all of the pace from it - and even when there was a problem in qualifying that compromised the rear ride height he made the best of it. 
- Considering he was on the back foot after missing FP1, it was a well-worked weekend.
CONS
- Two offs at the first chicane, one at the start of his final Q3 run that meant he lost the tow to the McLarens and another during the race, the main negatives.
Verdict: Got everything he could out of the Red Bull package.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/McLAREN_LN.png)
Started: 8th Finished: 4th
PROS
- Drove intelligently in battle, exemplified by out-deploying Piastri to prevail in their battle for fourth on the last lap.
- While the qualifying result was disappointing, there's an asterisk against it in that Piastri's first-chicane error cost him a tow.
CONS
- Wasn't consistent in executing qualifying laps, which contributed to being only eighth on the grid.
Verdict: Marginally the more accomplished McLaren driver despite qualifying disappointment.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/HAAS_OB.png)
Started: 11th Finished: 15th
PROS
- Adapted well to the upgraded aerodynamic package of the Haas, and also benefitted from having the new Ferrari power unit.
- His race pace was good, and his overall result would have been better had the VSC not been deployed just as he passed the pit entry, making a stop impossible.
- Made gains at both starts.
CONS
- Failed to improve on his second Q2 lap, meaning he didn't get the most out of the Haas despite a decent overall result.
- Compromised himself slightly by pushing a little too hard to stay with Yuki Tsunoda - but ultimately he needed to do that to maximise the chance of a point.
- Lost a place to Colapinto when he was jumped at the VSC restart.
Verdict: A strong performance on a track where even the upgraded Haas wasn't a points-scorer.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/FERRARI_LH.png)
Started: 4th Finished: 6th
PROS
- Although he struggled with the car more than Leclerc early in the weekend, he recovered well.
- Final Q3 lap, just seven-thousandths off Leclerc, ensured he salvaged a good position from what had been a very difficult qualifying.
CONS
- Had an untidy qualifying, albeit not entirely of his making.
- Turn 1 move on Leclerc was perfectly legitimate, but it put him in a high-risk position for Turn 2 and he paid the price for that. Not the ideal trade-off of risk-versus-reward given how the racing was expected to pan out and it cost him significant ground, albeit with the caveat he might have expected his team-mate to give him the necessary space.
- Cut the first chicane on lap 35, allowing Antonelli past.
Verdict: A patchy weekend, but Ferrari itself played a big part in that.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/AUDI_GB.png)
Started: 10th Finished: 11th
PROS
- Showed good pace in the Audi throughout the weekend at a track that played to the car's weaknesses.
- Realistically, 11th place was probably about where an Audi should finish even though there was perhaps an opportunity to have beaten Tsunoda.
- Passed Nico Hulkenberg in the race to secure lead-Audi honours.
CONS
- A small mistake at Ascari on his final Q2 lap cost him a place in Q3.
- A poor second start cost him, and despite Audi's launch troubles it was significantly worse than Hulkenberg's. Conversely, he had made a better first than Hulkenberg.
- Pace-wise, Tsunoda was beatable to the last point but only if Bortoleto hadn't lost track position at the second start.
Verdict: The stronger Audi driver, but with a few untidy moments.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/RED-BULL_LL.png)
Started: 22nd (pits) Finished: 14th
PROS
- Power unit component changes mean he was always on the back foot this weekend given he had a grid penalty.
- Couldn't have done much to avoid the front-wing damage sustained on the restart lap - given that was the result of Hulkenberg chopping across him on the run to Turn 1.
- Although comparisons are difficult, Lawson's pace was more than respectable and there's no doubt he would have scored well with a clean race, even from the pitlane start.
CONS
- The circumstances of the weekend in terms of the grid penalty and the front wing damage - which forced a pitstop that disconnected him from the field - meant the opportunities to impress were limited.
- He was given a black-and-white warning flag for squeezing Hulkenberg onto the grass approaching the second chicane, but that came with no associated penalty and was a harsh marginal call anyway.
Verdict: Another decent stand-in performance, even if the results don't show it.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/McLAREN_OP.png)
Started: 6th Finished: 5th
PROS
- Drove a clean race and for the most part played his hand well in battle.
- While he has struggled at times with race pace recently, including last time out at Zandvoort, he and Norris were well-matched at Monza.
- First Q3 lap was strong and allowed him to outqualify Norris, albeit partly because of his own error on the second run.
CONS
- Felt he could have prevailed in the last-lap battle with Norris for fourth place, saying "I know what I'd do differently".
- While he was put into a difficult situation and the stewards justifiably concluded he had "no other options available" and "inadvertently" blocked Lawson at the first chicane in Q3, earning himself a three-place grid drop, it has to be considered a very minor negative given there's usually something the driver can do to avoid such outcomes.
- Chicane lock-up on his final Q3 run ruined his final lap.
Verdict: A much-needed weekend of even pace across conditions.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/RB_YT.png)
Started: 15th Finished: 10th
PROS
- His Q1 exit was partly down to what he described as technical problems that he battled during Friday and Saturday, so that's a mitigating factor.
- Drove a good, incisive race to climb to take a point.
- Of the three drivers who ran from the restart to the finish on mediums, his pace stood up the best in relative terms.
CONS
- His inexperience with the quirks of the power units troubled him at times and contributed to what went wrong in qualifying.
- While he escaped without penalty for confusing which side of the grid he was restarting on, which the team must take some responsibility for, there remains some jeopardy given Audi's intended appeal.
Verdict: Raced well to salvage a good result from a challenging weekend.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/WILLIAMS_AA.png)
Started: 20th Finished: 17th
PROS
- Played the team game both in qualifying and the race, in the latter case also ensuring Sainz got overtake mode to harvest extra energy.
- Was making a de facto non-stop run on hards work, only to have to make a late precautionary stop because of vibrations.
- His underlying race pace was good despite the disappointing result.
CONS
- Not his fault so it doesn't directly count against him, but power unit component changes and the resulting 20-place grid penalty reduced him to a tow-provider in qualifying and cost the opportunity to show his true single-lap speed.
- Circumstances made it more difficult for him to make an impression.
Verdict: A better weekend than the results suggest.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/HAAS_EB.png)
Started: 14th Finished: 16th
PROS
- Had the dual disadvantages of not having the upgraded Ferrari engine and being the Haas driver to suffer from the aerodynamic problems that seem to blight one car or the other.
- Given the car wasn't working well, his qualifying pace was decent.
- A great first start briefly got him into the points.
CONS
- It's difficult to make a fair evaluation of his pace given the power unit-spec difference and the fact his car wasn't working as it should do aerodynamically.
Verdict: Machinery limited his opportunity to show what he could do, and his ranking has to reflect that.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/CADILLAC_SP.png)
Started: 17th Finished: 18th
PROS
- Drove a good race to win the Cadillac battle after jumping Bottas at the first start.
- Covered Alonso well in their battle in the first part of the race.
CONS
- Was behind Bottas in qualifying by 0.231s, although there were mitigating factors for that.
- Picked up a five-second penalty for failing to follow the prescribed route in the first chicane run-off area, which didn't affect his position but was needless.
Verdict: Disappointing in qualifying, but more effective in the race.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/CADILLAC_VB.png)
Started: 16th Finished: 19th
PROS
- Through no fault of his own, lost around 10s in the VSC pitstop as the second car in a double-stack where both stops were slow.
- Had the edge on Perez in qualifying.
- His race pace fundamentally was decent.
CONS
- Lost position to Perez at the first start, although that was largely down to circumstances rather than any major error on his part.
- Falling into blue-flag territory earlier led to him losing more time than Perez.
Verdict: A good weekend, with the 32-second gap to Perez at the finish misleading.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/AUDI_NH.png)
Started: 12th Finished: 12th
PROS
- For the most part drove a good race, including a decent second start, which is no easy thing in an Audi.
- Came through well after making a stop under the VSC, following Bortoleto home.
CONS
- Off at the first chicane allowed Colapinto to pass him during the race.
- Didn't execute qualifying especially well, ending up 0.262s behind his team-mate.
- A brief "sitting duck" phase in the race that he struggled to explain, likely related to deployment, cost him track position and compromised his chance of scoring.
Verdict: A solid weekend, but he was the second-best Audi driver overall.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/ALPINE_FC.png)
Started: 7th Finished: 9th
PROS
- At times, he showed good pace.
- Did a superb job at the two starts to turn seventh on the original grid to, all-too-briefly, third place.
- Kept his head down in recovery to salvage a couple of points. His ninth place potentially was only one place worse than he would have been without the mistake - but he was much further back on time than he should have been.
CONS
- Couldn't match Gasly's pace evolution in qualifying, dropping from 0.050s behind in Q1 to 0.323s in Q2, then the final 0.434s.
- Admitted to there being corners that "troubled me" in qualifying, primarily the second chicane and Ascari - where his trend for being more attacking on the brakes and a bit later on the power proved a disadvantage when the energy demands were factored in.
- His Lesmo off was hugely costly, both in terms of positions and the floor damage he sustained.
Verdict: A missed opportunity, although he did at least salvage a reasonable result.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/ASTON-MARTIN_FA.png)
Started: 21st (pits) Finished: DNF
PROS
- Extracted what pace he could from the car, outqualifying Lance Stroll despite having to rely on his first Q1 run thanks to power unit problems intervening.
- Raced well in the early stages to take the fight to the Cadillacs.
CONS
- He took responsibility for a wide moment that gave him damage and led to his retirement because, as he put it, "we were slow and with damage on the car, no point".
Verdict: Did what he could with the Aston Martin, but ranking is hurt given he took responsibility for the damage that led to his retirement.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/ASTON-MARTIN_LS.png)
Started: 18th Finished: DNF
PROS
- Wasn't in any way responsible for his retirement with a hydraulics failure.
- Largely drove cleanly through the weekend.
CONS
- While the 0.072s deficit to Alonso looks decent on paper, that was a clean session compared to his team-mate's curtailed one with the laptime set on scrubbed softs.
- Lost the tow early in the race, which Alonso was able to stay in.
Verdict: Had nothing to work with, but still did less with it than Alonso.
![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/dd/af/ddafbd99-2ccd-468c-b622-4b3cccf80b49/content/images/2026/09/FERRARI_CL.png)
Started: 3rd Finished: DNF
PROS
- Did a better job than Hamilton in qualifying, albeit in the final reckoning only by the narrowest of margins.
CONS
- Parabolica shunt at the end of lap two was a big error, especially given he'd made a similar mistake there in the 2020 race - albeit with the added complication this time of it being during battle.
- While he mentioned the "difference in power delivery" from lap one to lap two as a contributing factor to the crash, that comes with the territory with these power units.
- Given it was his team-mate, could have been more judicious at Turn 2 on the first lap.
Verdict: Quick, but race shunt was a major error.
summary: Edd Straw's 2026 Italian Grand Prix driver rankings highlight a memorable weekend of racing action at Monza, featuring standout performances and notable strategic challenges up and down the grid. Drivers like Antonelli managed to secure unexpected victories despite late race errors, while others like Gasly capitalized cleanly on qualifying pace. The comprehensive assessment details the highs and lows of the field, noting how varying car packages, grid penalties, and race incidents shaped each driver's final result.
key_points: Antonelli overcame starting 19th and a late gravel excursion to claim an unexpected win at Monza.
Gasly executed a near-flawless qualifying session and drove intelligently to finish seventh as the top midfield runner.
Max Verstappen extracted maximum pace from the Red Bull package to secure a third-place finish despite missing FP1 and dealing with car issues.
Lewis Hamilton experienced a patchy weekend involving a risky Turn 1 move with his teammate and a chicane cut, ultimately finishing sixth.
Liam Lawson delivered a respectable stand-in performance, advancing from a pitlane start to finish 14th despite suffering front-wing damage.

title: Joshua vs Fury: Tyson Fury says he is looking for new opponent and calls out Oleksandr Usyk
author: Ben Collins
content:
![Tyson Fury holds up his hand and is wearing a boxing glove and Anthony Joshua holds up two fingers and has a Union Jack over his shoulders](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/637e/live/bd065030-9d53-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.png)
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have signed contracts with Saudi Arabian promoter Sela to fight each other
- Published
Tyson Fury claims he is looking for a new opponent for November and has called out Oleksandr Usyk despite being contracted to fight Anthony Joshua next.
The all-British heavyweight showdown is being targeted for November, with both Joshua and Fury signing individual contracts for the contest.
But the issue of where the fight takes place has caused a delay in an official announcement with organisers pushing to stage it in the US rather than Joshua's preferred location of Wembley Stadium.
In an expletive-laden video posted on Instagram, Fury claimed Joshua was backing out of the fight.
"This will only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk," he said.
"Oleksandr you're his [Joshua's] trainer and his sensei and you know he is weak minded... and that he would never fight the Gypsy King which you have had the guts to do twice.
"You got the decisions last time, fair play to you.
"Good luck to you, let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court... do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits?
"Let me know because I am now looking for a new opponent."
However, Usyk's manager Sergey Lapin says the Ukrainian "is not Tyson's back-up plan".
In a statement to Sky Sports News, Lapin said: "Oleksandr is always open to big challenges. But serious intentions are backed by a concrete offer, not statements in the press."
Fury has twice lost to Usyk, with the two-time undisputed heavyweight champion now working with Joshua as part of his training and coaching team.
Sela, Queensberry and Matchroom declined to comment on whether talks had broken down when contacted by BBC Sport.
Saudi Arabian promoter Sela is fronting the bill for the prospective Joshua-Fury fight, with both men signing separate contracts with the company.
Joshua's contract stipulates it must take place in the UK, leading to his promoter Eddie Hearn renegotiating details in that deal.
But after London Mayor Sir Sadiq Khan made a public plea for the fight to happen at Wembley, Hearn said talks about staging it in the UK had "re-opened".
Sela and broadcaster Netflix are understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden.
BBC Sport understands Sela has contacted the London mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium, but have not progressed talks further since last week.
Hearn had said he hoped an announcement could happen in the coming week, but that now seems unlikely given the latest developments.
A bout at Wembley may need to happen in the early hours - which would draw in a larger television audience in the US.
Khan says his team would back such a proposal.
"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.
"I'm hoping the promoters understand that not only will you get 100,000 people watching this bout live, you'll get millions watching it across the globe, where both boxers are cheered on by their loyal fans."
summary: Tyson Fury claims he is seeking a new opponent for November and has called out Oleksandr Usyk, accusing Anthony Joshua of backing out of their targeted bout. While Joshua and Fury have signed contracts with promoter Sela, the fight has been delayed by disagreements over whether it should take place at Wembley Stadium or in the United States. Usyk's manager stated that the Ukrainian is not a backup plan and requires a concrete offer rather than press statements.
key_points: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have signed individual contracts with Saudi Arabian promoter Sela for a prospective November heavyweight fight.
The fight announcement has been delayed because Joshua prefers the bout at Wembley Stadium, while organisers and broadcaster Netflix favor New York's Madison Square Garden.
Fury released a video claiming Joshua is backing out and called out Oleksandr Usyk for a November fight.
Usyk's manager, Sergey Lapin, stated that Usyk is not a backup plan and requires a concrete offer.
London Mayor Sadiq Khan has publicly expressed a desire to host the fight at Wembley Stadium.

title: US Open 2026 results: Zheng Qinwen shocks Iga Swiatek to reach quarter-finals
author: Phil Cartwright
content:
![Zheng Qinwen drops to the floor in celebration](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/18f3/live/cbabd780-aae7-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Zheng Qinwen has matched her best ever performance at the US Open by reaching the quarter-finals
- Published
Zheng Qinwen won a set from 5-0 down for the second match in succession as she extended her fantastic US Open run by beating former champion Iga Swiatek to reach the quarter-finals.
Zheng, the reigning Olympic champion and former world number four, dropped outside the world's top 100 earlier this year while struggling to regain her best form following elbow surgery in July 2025.
The 23-year-old from China had trailed Madison Keys 5-0 in the deciding set of their third-round match on Saturday before winning seven successive games to secure her spot in round four.
And Zheng was 5-0 down in the opening set against Poland's eighth seed Swiatek, but won 13 of the next 16 games on Arthur Ashe Stadium to set up a quarter-final against either Naomi Osaka or Elena Rybakina.
The second set was on serve until the seventh game, when Zheng crushed a powerful backhand return winner to secure a crucial break, and she broke again two games later to complete a 7-5 6-3 victory.
This latest win - her seventh in a row in New York having come through three rounds of qualifying - will put her back to the brink of the top 50.
"The more matches I play, the more rhythm I have on court," said Zheng.
"People have asked me if I'm tired and when I arrived I was not tired at all. I felt really pumped for my match, trying to reach better levels here and enjoy this fantastic stadium."
Elsewhere, French Open winner Mirra Andreeva recovered from losing the first set to Austria's Anastasia Potapova to reach the last eight in New York for the first time in her career.
The year of the qualifier?
Zheng's only win in eight previous meetings against Swiatek was in the semi-finals of the 2024 Olympics on her way to singles gold in Paris.
She will discover her quarter-final opponent later on Monday, when former US Open champion Osaka plays second seed Rybakina.
Former world number five Daniela Hantuchova told BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra: "She [Zheng] is starting to be very dangerous for the rest of the players left.
"I don't want to say she's playing the best tennis out of everyone, but if you have Iga Swiatek panicking on the other side of the court, not knowing what to do, that says a lot."
The most recent qualifier to reach this stage of the women's draw at the US Open was Great Britain's Emma Raducanu, who went on to win the title in 2021.
And Zheng is not the first female qualifier to perform well at a Grand Slam in 2026 - Poland's Maja Chwalinska, who began the French Open at 114th in the world, lost to Russian teenager Andreeva in the final at Roland Garros.
Swiatek 'started making mistakes' after fast start
For Swiatek, 25, a fourth-round exit is a disappointing end to her Grand Slam season, with a quarter-final appearance at the Australian Open her best result.
She was beaten in round four of the French Open, while the defence of her Wimbledon title ended in the third round.
It means that, for the first time since 2021, Swiatek will end a year without winning one of the sport's four majors.
Swiatek, who received treatment to her left thigh when leading 2-1 in the second set, had entered the US Open in excellent form by winning the WTA 1000 event in Toronto and getting to the semi-finals in Cincinnati, while she had progressed through to round four without dropping a set.
Reflecting on losing the first set to Zheng, Swiatek said she simply missed too many shots after going 5-0 up.
"My focus was the same as always," said the six-time major winner. "I wanted to play the same as always. [I] just started to miss too much, wanted to adjust it, but nothing kind of worked at that point.
"I knew I was going to have another chance and I wanted to use it, but I missed them all."
She continued: "I wouldn't say it had anything to do with mentality. It was more that I started making mistakes from easy balls and Qinwen stopped doing mistakes. She played the balls better."
Andreeva through against 'warrior' Potapova
![Mirra Andreeva consoles Anastasia Potapova](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/9f9f/live/9ec4c920-aae7-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Andreeva consoled an emotional Potapova at the end of their fourth-round match
Andreeva, 19, was severely tested by Potapova until the 24th seed injured her knee in what proved to be the final game of their match on Louis Armstrong Stadium.
Potapova seemed to twist or hyperextend her knee while attempting to hit a ball on the run from the baseline and Andreeva was across quickly to check on her grounded opponent.
Potapova returned to the court after receiving treatment but lost the remaining points in her service game, confirming her exit from the tournament.
Fifth seed Andreeva, who won 5-7 6-4 6-3, said: "Anastasia is my good friend and seeing what a battle we had and seeing her fall like that in the last game, it's not easy.
"I told her that she's been playing amazing and having one of her best seasons. I'm sure she'll come back even stronger - she's a warrior and an even better fighter than me."
Andreeva will play either Coco Gauff or Iva Jovic, who play their all-American fourth-round match in Monday's night session, in the quarter-finals.
summary: Zheng Qinwen reached the US Open quarter-finals by defeating former champion Iga Swiatek 7-5 6-3, overcoming a 5-0 deficit in the opening set for the second consecutive match. The reigning Olympic champion has won seven matches in a row at the tournament after coming through the qualifying rounds. Meanwhile, French Open winner Mirra Andreeva advanced to the last eight after her opponent, Anastasia Potapova, suffered a knee injury in the final game.
key_points: Zheng Qinwen beat Iga Swiatek 7-5 6-3 after recovering from a 5-0 deficit in the first set.
Zheng entered the tournament through qualifying and has won seven consecutive matches in New York.
The defeat means Iga Swiatek will end a year without a major title for the first time since 2021.
Mirra Andreeva reached the quarter-finals following a three-set victory over Anastasia Potapova, who sustained a late knee injury.

title: ‘Relief’ of Premier League title has given Arsenal confidence, says David Raya
author: David Hytner
content:
David Raya says Arsenal are playing with greater confidence after the “relief” of winning the Premier League. The champions continued their perfect start to the defence of their crown with the 2-1 home win over Chelsea on Sunday, making it nine points out of nine.
It was a powerhouse performance coloured by a freedom of expression, which stood in contrast to the nerviness of the final months of last season when the team laboured under a weight of pressure and expectation before they beat Manchester City to the title. That was Arsenal’s first triumph since 2004 and followed three consecutive runners-up finishes.
The shackles were off against Chelsea, just as they have been for much of the season, beginning with the 3-0 win over City in the Community Shield. Kai Havertz and Martin Ødegaard scored the goals against Chelsea and provided most of the creative flourishes. But it was the ferocity of the collective intensity, the sheer physicality, that took the breath. Raya pulled off a stunning late save to deny the Chelsea substitute Estêvão. Arsenal did not deserve to drop points. It was an ominous statement of intent from them.
“Winning the league after that many years and after those years that you are so close … it gives you that relief and it gives you that extra confidence,” Raya said. “Coming from the three games this season, especially the Community Shield, winning against City, the way we played against them – that gives you extra motivation and extra confidence to play the way we want to play …
“Hopefully we can keep playing this way because we know how good we are. We know we can beat anybody in this league. Let’s just focus on the moment and be in the present.”
The most eye-catching aspect of the display was how Arsenal reacted to going behind after 77 seconds to a Morgan Rogers volley. They attacked in waves and created a remarkable number of openings before Havertz equalised in the 25th minute. The belief could also be felt in the stands where there was no panic, only bellowed encouragement.
“There’s things to improve on that goal [by Rogers],” Raya said. “We had to defend a little bit better, especially right at the start of the game. It was disappointing to concede that goal. But the main thing is the reaction that we had after it and the way we played. The way we dominated, the way we attacked, we defended.
after newsletter promotion
“We know how good Chelsea are, especially in transitions, and the way the play is dragged back to defend. So it was a really important win.”
summary: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya believes the relief of winning their first Premier League title since 2004 has given the team extra confidence and freedom this season. The champions maintained their perfect start to their title defense with a 2-1 home win over Chelsea, overcoming an early goal from Morgan Rogers. Raya made a crucial late save to secure the victory, highlighting Arsenal's strong collective intensity and physical performance.
key_points: Arsenal defeated Chelsea 2-1 to achieve nine points from their first three games of the season.
David Raya stated that winning the Premier League has brought the team relief and boosted their confidence.
Arsenal successfully recovered after conceding a goal to Morgan Rogers just 77 seconds into the match.
Kai Havertz and Martin Ødegaard scored the goals and drove Arsenal's creative play against Chelsea.

title: FPL notes: Most-sold Mbeumo scores, Rashford, Garner + Norgaard injury latest
author: Avfc
content:
Everton snatched a point against Manchester United on Sunday, with Gameweek 3’s most-sold player, Bryan Mbeumo (£7.9m), on the scoresheet.
Here are our Scout Notes from the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
- READ MORE: FPL notes: £4.5m midfielder praise + another Hull clean sheet
- READ MORE: FPL notes: Jaissle on Fernandez-Pardo’s fitness + Wissa deeper
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-173.png)
MBEUMO PUNISHES SELLERS
Dumped by over 1m Fantasy managers ahead of Gameweek 3, Mbeumo netted for the second successive match.
After a quiet first-half, the 27-year-old drifted between two Everton players and placed it into the bottom corner with a quality finish.
Prior to that, he almost supplied an assist, too, when Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) struck the crossbar from his headed knockdown.
Overall, this was another positive display from Mbeumo, who has now produced 19 points in his last two matches.
Substitute Benjamin Sesko (£7.0m) later looked like he’d got the winner with a powerful header from Luke Shaw’s (£4.5m) superb delivery, but for the third successive week, United let in two goals.
If Michael Carrick’s men are to build on last season’s third-place finish, they surely need to tighten up defensively.
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-174.png)
Above: Teams sorted by goals conceded (GC) in Gameweek 1-3
RASHFORD SHARP… BUT IS HE INJURED?
While Fernandes and Matheus Cunha (£7.9m) were both below par on Merseyside, Marcus Rashford (£7.0m) looked really sharp.
A constant outlet down the left flank, he caused Merlin Rohl (£5.0m) so many problems.
On Sunday’s evidence, it’s surely only a matter of time before he delivers his first attacking return of the season.
“Yeah, he’s done very well. As I said during the week, he’s done ever so well since he came back. I thought he looked really sharp again today and dangerous. That final little moment didn’t quite drop for him, but nevertheless, I thought he created really good opportunities, and there was a big threat throughout the game.
“I think you’re trying to build those partnerships and combinations throughout the team, really, and they’ve played together [Rashford and Shaw] for quite some time now and have an understanding. Marcus and Luke, were particularly dangerous down that side.” – Michael Carrick on Marcus Rashford
However, Rashford was taken off in the 70th minute. Before that, he appeared to be complaining to the bench about a possible injury.
“Yeah, he was feeling a bit of something.” – Michael Carrick on Marcus Rashford
Carrick should next face the media on Wednesday, ahead of the Champions League trip to face Sabah.
After that, of course, it’s the Manchester derby in Gameweek 4.
Elsewhere, Kobbie Mainoo (£5.5m) impressed again in the middle of the park. He supplied the assist for Mbeumo’s strike and racked up 15 defensive contributions (DefCon) for the second successive week.
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-175.png)
EVERTON SUBS DELIVER
Everton had a transfer deadline day to forget, but Jack Grealish (£6.5m) did at least arrive on loan, while Ainsley Maitland-Niles (£4.5m) also joined the group.
They both started on the bench here.
“We’ve needed him, but he is not where he should be fitness wise yet.” – David Moyes on Jack Grealish prior to the match
However, both Grealish and Maitland-Niles played key roles in the Toffees’ comeback.
Grealish replaced the ineffective Brennan Johnson (£5.9m) in the second-half and was really lively after he subbed on.
Maitland-Niles meanwhile nicked a point with the last kick, picking out the top corner from about 25 yards.
Another substitute, Hayden Hackney (£5.5m), supplied the assist for Tyrique George’s (£5.5m) excellent strike, so perhaps Everton have a bit more squad depth than we initially thought.
“He’s a young player. Today he was a problem for them at different times. His finish was very good when we needed it. He’ll get better and continue to improve.” – David Moyes on Tyrique George
Everton’s unbeaten record this season remains intact, then.
They take on Tottenham Hotspur in Gameweek 4, before back-to-back matches against newly-promoted opposition, Ipswich Town and Hull City.
BARRY WASTEFUL
Despite those positives, Thierno Barry (£5.5m) was wasteful in front of goal.
He’s the club’s only senior striker after the sale of Beto, but although he worked hard and made some decent runs, he headed over a big chance from Rohl’s whipped delivery.
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-176.png)
Above: Thierno Barry’s expected goals (xG) shot map v Man Utd
Remember, Barry also missed two big chances at Bournemouth in Gameweek 2.
He is at least getting opportunities, however.
Indeed, excluding penalties, only Erling Haaland (£15.5m) has generated more xG this season than Barry.
GARNER + NORGAARD LATEST
James Garner (£6.0m), who spent most of the summer on the sidelines after hernia surgery, went down in the second half and couldn’t continue.
But when discussing Maitland-Niles, David Moyes told reporters it was only cramp, rather than an injury.
We haven’t had much chance to get to know him. We were going to keep Jimmy [Garner] at right-back but he cramped up, but it was a brilliant goal, a great finish. Brilliantly struck, pleased for him. It’s a good start for him and it will help him settle in as well.” – David Moyes on Ainsley Maitland-Niles and James Garner
Christian Norgaard (£4.9m) meanwhile is unlikely to feature before the international break.
“No, we don’t, no [when asked if we’ll see Norgaard before the international break]. I think we knew it might be something that would keep him out. We hoped it might have been quicker but it’s not. But he’s just beginning to make a little more progress now which is pleasing because we need his experience and the extra bodies moving forward.” – David Moyes on Christian Norgaard
MATCH ANALYSIS
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-177.png)
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/5-Flash-Sale-Graphic.jpg)
summary: Everton and Manchester United played to a draw after substitute Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored a late equalizer with the final kick of the game. Gameweek 3's most-sold player, Bryan Mbeumo, scored his second successive goal for United, while Marcus Rashford showed a sharp performance before being substituted due to feeling an issue. Everton substitutes Jack Grealish and Maitland-Niles both made significant impacts in their team's comeback.
key_points: Bryan Mbeumo scored for the second consecutive match after being dumped by over one million Fantasy managers ahead of Gameweek 3.
Marcus Rashford played well on the left flank but was subbed off in the 70th minute after complaining of a possible injury to the bench.
Everton substitutes Jack Grealish and Ainsley Maitland-Niles played key roles in securing a draw, with Maitland-Niles scoring from 25 yards out.
David Moyes confirmed that James Garner's second-half exit was due to cramp rather than a serious injury.
Christian Norgaard is unlikely to feature for Everton before the upcoming international break.

title: Wild opening salvo against Chelsea hints at exciting times for Arsenal fans | Barney Ronay
author: Barney Ronay
content:
We’re back, baby. So, so back. Well, OK, not exactly back. But back down the time tunnel, for a while at least, as on a powder blue afternoon at the Emirates Stadium, Arsenal and Chelsea produced an opening half-hour that felt like a throwback to prime Barclays of the early 2000s.
In that period this really did feel like a twist on a classic: spells of midfield murder-ball, stretched and flustered full‑backs, players hurling themselves at the defensive lines like the fall guys in a cowboy western being tossed out through the saloon-bar doors.
Arsenal had 10 shots in that period and played breathless, physically overwhelming attacking football. The game settled after they scored their equaliser. In the second half it became simply gripping and episodic, broken up by subs and stoppages, which is the current dynamic. Second halves: these are a problem. But Arsenal never really looked like losing their 2-1 lead.
The key to the day was that agreeably wild opening half‑hour, evidence that both teams have will and the energy to progress this season. Which will, in turn, be good news for the Premier League.
About last season. It was OK, wasn’t it? Quite a lot of demo-mode football. Games that were like watching someone knitting a scarf. Teams with such elite levels of defensive organisation the experience is like watching one of those police motorbike display teams doing a pyramid, while a group of men on laptops furiously study the data.
All very orderly, and disciplined. Just lacking in colour and fire. And more significantly, the higher gears that mean you might actually be able to run step for step with Paris Saint-Germain, or blow away, rather than slowly strangle, an opponent.
It is about balance of course, about releasing the urge for total control. There was a moment on 87 minutes that captured both sides of this. Chelsea were awarded a free-kick 25 yards out in front of goal: high drama, a moment to be seized, necks craned forward in the seats. At which point Danny Welbeck, on as a late sub, sprinted straight to Reece James as he prepared to shoot, looking like a man in a state of high alert, some vital mission being run. Welbeck’s mission turned out to be handing James a piece of paper and urging him to read it. What was this? Expected 87th-minute free-kick numbers? Forty-seven per cent scoring chance uplift high and to the left? Maybe it just said “Score, dufus”, in which case, more of this please. James studied it dutifully, then paced out his run again. And to be fair, if the note did say hammer it straight into Declan Rice’s head, then job done, great process everyone. But the overriding feeling was: no, thank you. Away with you, interventionist wonks, tracksuited control freakery. This is art. This is play, this is drama. Whatever it is, it’s definitely not time for a briefing.
![Kai Havertz scores](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/518edf74a2d224e38880bc50e6b35faa989d5355/0_0_2949_1850/master/2949.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The other thing, simultaneous to this, was Morgan Rogers walking off around the pitch and being barracked relentlessly by the Arsenal fans – “You should have signed for a big club” – but looking spent, exhausted and emotionally drained, after giving everything to that part of the spectacle that felt like the counterpoint to Welbeck’s note, the wildness and the energy that feeds this thing.
There really was nothing not to like about that start, which was all jam, all sugar rush. First there was the manager match‑up, a kind of Basque childhood romcom revenge drama. The league needs rivalries and sibling symmetry. It feeds off this stuff. Hmm. They might have to start jabbing each other in the chest a bit more. But it was still fascinating to see Xabi Alonso on the touchline. This was fresh meat for the eye: jawline, pecs, tan, elite smart-casual styling, and above all an effortless sense of aura. There’s a new sheriff in town. Even the sun had appeared, giving off a weird, dead September heat, the sky behind the stand a pale Hockney blue. And Chelsea scored with 1min 17sec gone, Rogers finishing on the volley with a measured, very deliberate grubber into the corner.
For a while these two teams just ran into each other. Emi Martínez was kicked in the head but got up and was still booed relentlessly. Arsenal had a goal disallowed. They produced one flowing full-length move, set up by a lovely roll and spin by Myles Lewis‑Skelly. On 25 minutes it was 1-1, the goal all Kai Havertz’s own work as he drifted inside like a gangling, bookish Arjen Robben then shot low inside the near post.
after newsletter promotion
Havertz was also involved in the decisive moment, producing a lovely, and indeed deeply unfashionable dummy to put Martin Ødegaard in space in front of goal. It wasn’t even really a dummy, Havertz just dribbled his foot away, with no real feint or shoulder dip in the classic dummy style.
Arsenal’s fans are sometimes frustrated by Ødegaard. He’s not direct enough, doesn’t shoot, always gilding the lily, regilding it, taking it back to the gilders for another look. Maybe this is how you get him to shoot. Put him right in front of goal with time to see every option, run the numbers, and conclude, ‘oh, well, I really am going to have to do this?’
The finish was emphatic. After that the game became snarling and mean for a bit. Arsenal did enter one of their slow periods, taking the air out of it, killing the game a bit. But this was an excellent win against a very promising Chelsea.
A final thought. The question will be asked: why don’t Arsenal always play like this? Why stop with the rage and forward gallops? The answer is that you can’t. It’s physically very hard. This is not a computer game. They’re humans, with 90 minutes to run. The real question is, can you raise it again, take that 30-minute spell and store it away, keep it ready in your repertoire? If so, and on the evidence here, we really might have an Arsenal upgrade on our hands.
summary: Arsenal secured a 2-1 win against Chelsea following a wild, high-energy opening half-hour that offered a throwback to early 2000s football. After Chelsea's early goal by Morgan Rogers, Arsenal equalized through Kai Havertz and later took the lead via Martin Ødegaard. Although the game slowed down in the second half, Arsenal successfully maintained their advantage to claim an excellent victory.
key_points: Arsenal and Chelsea produced a breathless, physically overwhelming opening 30 minutes featuring 10 shots from Arsenal.
Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for Chelsea with a volley just over a minute into the match.
Kai Havertz scored Arsenal's equalizer and later provided a crucial dummy to set up Martin Ødegaard for the winning goal.
Arsenal never looked like losing their 2-1 lead despite the game becoming more fragmented and episodic in the second half.

title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard shine for Gunners
author: Neil Johnston
content:
Champions Arsenal come from behind to beat Chelsea
- Published
Arsenal shelled out close to Â£200m on new signings during the summer transfer window but fell short of landing the elite forward they craved.
Former Manchester City goalscorer Julian Alvarez was on their radar but remains at Atletico Madrid, while the Gunners were also interested in Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers, Paris St-Germain's Bradley Barcola and Vinicius Jr.
While Rogers opted for London rivals Chelsea, Barcola moved to Liverpool and Vinicius Jr has stayed at Real Madrid.
Yet reigning champions Arsenal have started this season as strongly as they finished 2025-26, when they celebrated their first Premier League title for 22 years.
After wins over Coventry City and Aston Villa, they came from behind to beat big-spending Chelsea 2-1 in a thrilling derby on Sunday - thanks to goals from two familiar faces.
Kai Havertz, an Arsenal player since 2023, and Martin Odegaard, who joined in 2021, scored as they passed their first big test of the campaign against opponents who have spent close to Â£350m since the end of last season.
A maximum nine points from three games, one goal conceded and big players stepping up.
"I can't see anyone stopping Arsenal," former Premier League winner Chris Sutton told BBC Sport.
Odegaard 'desire' in Chelsea win impresses Rooney
'Our mentality is to keep fighting'
It is surely too early in the season to get carried away, and there are likely to be bigger tests ahead for Mikel Arteta's side.
But Arsenal have set down an early marker as they chase back-to-back Premier League crowns.
Along with Manchester City, they are one of only two clubs with a maximum nine points from three games.
After sweeping aside Coventry on the opening day of the season, they produced a mature performance to come away with all three points at Villa.
Against Chelsea, they had to find a different way to win after Â£117m signing Rogers fired Chelsea into a second-minute lead.
"Our mentality is to keep fighting. We have shown that many times," said captain Odegaard, who scored the 50th-minute winner after Havertz had equalised before half-time.
"We never want to concede early, but the reaction is top. We got our reward in the end and the response was brilliant.
"We showed our quality with and without the ball and the result reflects that."
Odegaard has scored three goals in four appearances in all competitions this season, after netting only once in 36 last term.
"It was a big game, massive game, tough opponent, and we got there in the end, so brilliant," he said.
Former Manchester United and England player Ashley Young said Odegaard's form will be key for Arsenal this season.
"He's just a joy to watch," Young told BBC Sport.
"He's exciting when he gets on the ball, he's allowing other players to get on the ball.
"The connection down the right side between him, Bukayo Saka and Havertz - it's just good to see when you've got players that know each other and build relationships in that way.
"Riccardo Calafiori has been brilliant from last season. He seems to me like he's the one that's got a free role in the team.
"It was his run, and he played it precisely, for the winning goal. He goes quickly, takes people out of the way. It's just clever. Arsenal deserved all three points."
Havertz said Odegaard was back to his "very best".
"He's an unbelievable player - we have seen that over the last years," said the Germany forward.
"He's going to help us a lot this season."
Gabriel was 'extremely lucky' to avoid red - Rooney
'Arsenal are a powerhouse'
Sutton said Arsenal are still ahead of the rest, despite their rivals spending hundreds of millions of pounds during the transfer window.
"They're such a powerhouse," said the former Blackburn and England striker.
"Chelsea are a good team, but Arsenal always find a way to win. Can you stop Arsenal? I don't think they [other Premier League teams] can."
Arsenal have won their opening three games of a top-flight campaign while conceding fewer than two goals (1) for the third time - after 1924-25, when they finished 20th, and 2003-04, when they went the season unbeaten.
They have also won eight league games in a row stretching back to last season.
Having seen off big-spending Chelsea, their next league match is at Sunderland on Saturday.
Before that Arsenal launch their Champions League campaign at Napoli on Wednesday.
Havertz said Arsenal will head to Italy with confidence high with after seeing off his former club Chelsea.
"Chelsea have an amazing squad, but so do we," said Havertz, who scored the winning goal for the Blues against Manchester City in the 2021 Champions League final.
"We knew it was going to be tough. They scored early, so it's not easy for us, but we believed in ourselves and changed the game around."
'We reacted in an amazing way' - Arteta on Arsenal's win in London derby
summary: Reigning champions Arsenal came from behind to defeat big-spending Chelsea 2-1 in a Premier League derby with goals from Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard. The victory marks Arsenal's third consecutive win to start the season, maintaining a maximum nine points. Mikel Arteta's side overcame an early second-minute goal from Morgan Rogers to secure the win.
key_points: Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 thanks to goals from Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard.
Morgan Rogers scored a second-minute goal for Chelsea before Arsenal fought back.
Arsenal has won their opening three games of the season, joining Manchester City on nine points.
Captain Martin Odegaard scored the 50th-minute winning goal, his third in four appearances this season.

title: Winners and losers from F1's memorable Italian Grand Prix
author: Filip Cleeren
content:
Winners and losers from F1's memorable Italian Grand Prix
As Kimi Antonelli wowed the Formula 1 paddock with his finest hour yet, his momentous home triumph in the Italian Grand Prix looks set to be a watershed moment for his maiden world championship chase
![Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes](https://cdn-9.motorsport.com/images/amp/24QGqX4Y/s1000/andrea-kimi-antonelli-mercedes.webp) 
Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images
Whether you are an adopted fan of Formula 1 2026's divisive yo-yo racing or not, you can't argue the Italian Grand Prix was short of things to pay attention to. Champion-elect - there, we said it - Kimi Antonelli served up a comeback race for the ages with the approval of the Ferrari tifosi, while the Scuderia itself tripped at the first hurdle at its home race.
Winner: Kimi Antonelli
Sunday looked set to be a day of conflicting emotions for the tifosi. Coming out in droves, and setting a new attendance record in the process, fans flocked to the Temple of Speed to worship Ferrari only to be left disappointed by what their national team served up.
But any tears after Charles Leclerc's violent accident on lap 2 soon made way for sheer joy and pride when Antonelli delivered a comeback race for the ages, taking a first Italian win at the country's home race since 1966.
After the finish the broadcasts showed a shot of scarlet-clad Ferrari fans holding up an Italian flag adorning Kimi's name, suggesting many of the sold-out crowd were able to swiftly pivot from revering their national institution to celebrating their new national hero.
Antonelli's masterclass yielded him the ultimate reward. Being greeted by a sea of fans on Monza's home stretch as he took the top step of the most glorious podium in F1. Unlike the Michael Schumacher years, though, that famous 1-2 two punch of the German and Italian national anthems was played it reverse order.
With the Monza box ticked off, surely the world championship one is next?
![Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes](https://cdn.motorsport.com/images/mgl/YWKAmWOY/s1000/andrea-kimi-antonelli-mercedes.jpg) 
Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images
Loser: George Russell
Antonelli's comeback was as spectacular for him as it was humbling for Russell, who all but waved the white flag at the end of the race when the championship odds were mentioned.
There wasn't a whole lot Russell did wrong, and if it hadn't been for Max Verstappen's qualifying antics who would have been on pole on Saturday. It just feels like he has met his match in his younger team-mate, and simply matching Antonelli will no longer be enough.
"Kimi is deserving to be in control of it," Russell said. "I'm not even thinking about a fight or a comeback or anything. It's going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap, so I'm just sort of accepting that is what it is."
A lot can happen in 10 races, but if Antonelli wasn't in cruise control already, then he landed a mental hammer blow in Monza.
Winner: Max Verstappen
Leave it to Verstappen to salvage a podium from a race he had little right to, fighting with one hand behind his back against the superior energy deployment of the Mercedes cars. Quite how Verstappen was able to scrap with Russell as long as he had, we have no idea.
But taking third, ahead of the two McLarens and despite clear issues with the RB22's rear axle, was the best possible result he could have hoped for. For a man who detests the type of battery-led yo-yo racing, surely a part of him must have enjoyed the jousting too.
![Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari](https://cdn.motorsport.com/images/mgl/2GdKvEEY/s1000/charles-leclerc-ferrari-lewis-.jpg) 
Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images
Loser: Ferrari
Ferrari came to its home race armed with its latest round of aerodynamic upgrades to make its car more efficient around the high-speed Monza blast, as well as its second permitted power unit upgrade that is thought to have slashed its horsepower deficit by 30-40%.
Despite an encouraging start on Friday, it wasn't quite enough when all dials were turned up to 11, though Ferrari's two-tenth deficit in qualifying on a power-hungry circuit suggested its progress was at least genuine.
But for a team that wanted to make steps with its race weekend execution, the race was another bruising experience with Leclerc at the centre of it. After being challenged by team-mate Lewis Hamilton on the inside of Turn 1 at the start, which became the outside for Turn 2, Leclerc drifted towards the exit as he forced Hamilton off.
Leclerc said he tried to "make Turn 2 as tight as I possibly could", but not quite tight enough to leave Hamilton any space as the Briton dropped to ninth. A simple race incident or a matter of Leclerc racing his team-mate harder than anyone else? It's only a question he can answer. But his race soon ended with a thud as he lost control of his car at the exit of Parabolica and smacked hard into the barriers on lap 2.
Ferrari was likely never going to defeat the Mercedes-engined cars on home turf, as evidenced by Hamilton being powerless to keep up with the frontrunners, but the tifosi surely expected better than sixth and a DNF.
Winner: Alpine
Following his sensational maiden pole on Saturday, Pierre Gasly couldn't quite keep up with the frontrunners on Sunday despite his best efforts to make life hard for Russell at the start, as he should.
Going from first to seventh doesn't sound too impressive in isolation, but Alpine did finish at the top of F1's midfield, which was the result it would have signed up for pre-weekend.
Franco Colapinto was in tears speaking to the media about his bizarre mistake at the first Lesmo that robbed him of an opportunity to be up there with Gasly, but he likely wouldn't have finished higher than eighth instead of ninth anyway.
In any case, Alpine will take a lot of morale from this weekend as it aims to regain control of the fight for fifth amid advances by Racing Bulls.
![Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing](https://cdn.motorsport.com/images/mgl/6lmAV4L0/s1000/lance-stroll-aston-martin-raci.jpg) 
Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing
Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images
Loser: Aston Martin - Honda
Aston Martin may have improved its car significantly in Hungary, but Honda's in-season improvements have been moderate at best and left the team completely exposed in Monza, disappearing behind Cadillac again.
Neither Fernando Alonso nor Lance Stroll made it to the finish, due to "suspected car damage" for the Spaniard and a hydraulic issue on the Canadian's machine.
2027 can't come soon enough for the Silverstone team.

From Formula 1 to MotoGP we report straight from the paddock because we love our sport, just like you. In order to keep delivering our expert journalism, our website uses advertising. Still, we want to give you the opportunity to enjoy an ad-free and tracker-free website and to continue using your adblocker.
summary: The Italian Grand Prix featured a memorable home victory for Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli following a stellar comeback race, bolstering his world championship lead. Meanwhile, Ferrari suffered a disappointing home weekend marked by Charles Leclerc crashing out on lap two and teammate Lewis Hamilton finishing sixth. Other notable performances included Max Verstappen salvaging a third-place podium finish and Alpine leading the midfield.
key_points: Kimi Antonelli won the Italian Grand Prix with a remarkable comeback drive, thrilling the local fans and strengthening his championship position.
Ferrari endured a difficult home race after Charles Leclerc crashed out on the second lap following an incident with teammate Lewis Hamilton, who ultimately finished sixth.
Max Verstappen secured a third-place podium finish despite facing challenges with his car's rear axle and Mercedes' energy deployment.
George Russell conceded that overcoming Antonelli's championship lead will be exceptionally challenging.
Alpine emerged at the top of the F1 midfield with Pierre Gasly finishing seventh.

title: Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Monza race from George Russell and Max Verstappen
author: Nigel Chiu
content:
Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Monza race from George Russell and Max Verstappen
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli became the first Italian to win at Monza since 1966 after an incredible drive from 19th to first; Antonelli had stunning pace to come through the field, then later caught George Russell in the closing laps; Max Verstappen claimed his fifth podium of 2026
Sunday 6 September 2026 17:09, UK
Kimi Antonelli completed a remarkable comeback to win his home Italian Grand Prix from 19th place after a race-long battle against Mercedes team-mate George Russell.
Antonelli was not expected to contend for victory due to grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation but stormed through the field early on - in between the red flag for Charles Leclerc's huge crash - and showed tremendous pace to catch Russell on an alternative strategy.
The two Mercedes and Max Verstappen pulled clear of the field in the first half of the race, exchanging the lead several times, due to the yoyo style of racing caused by the 2026 power units and the impact of having a slipstream around the long straights at Monza.

- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺
Antonelli and Verstappen pitted on Lap 29, just after half race distance, when a Virtual Safety Car came out for Lance Stroll stopping in his Aston Martin.
After their pit stops, the pair emerged in sixth and seventh with a 15-second deficit to Russell but comfortably made their way back up to the top positions on fresher tyres.
Antonelli caught Russell with five laps remaining but ran wide at the first chicane due to the track breaking up. However, he was soon back on Russell's tail and made the race-winning move with three laps to go, while Verstappen held off the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri to claim third.
It means Antonelli is 66 points ahead of Russell in the Drivers' Championship with the latter also expected to take grid penalties of his own at a future race.
"Unbelievable! "I am so happy and I could have never imagined to be here today," said Antonelli.
"But we managed to pull it off and I'm really, really happy."
Norris limited the damage in fourth on a weekend McLaren struggled, but not without a feisty battle with Piastri during the final laps, and is 96 points behind Antonelli in the standings.
Ferrari had huge hopes to win at Monza but Lewis Hamilton struggled to sixth, having been left frustrated since the opening lap when he was forced into the gravel by team-mate Leclerc who crashed hard on the third lap.
Pole-sitter Pierre Gasly did not have the pace and dropped to seventh, ahead of Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, his Alpine team-mate Franco Colapinto and the other Racing Bulls of Yuki Tsunoda.
How Antonelli completed stunning comeback
Mercedes had already planned an alternative strategy for Antonelli by starting him on the hard tyres and the championship leader made a phenomenal start to go from 19th to 12th in the three laps before Leclerc's huge shunt at the high-speed final corner.
Leclerc gingerly walked away from the accident but the race was red flagged so the barriers could be repaired, which allowed everyone to switch tyres.
Russell was on pole for the restart after he took the lead on the second lap from original pole-sitter Gasly, while Verstappen made up two spots and was third.
Most drivers put on the hard tyres but Verstappen, Hamilton who was eighth after being edged into the gravel by Leclerc on the first lap, and Antonelli were among six drivers to choose the mediums.
Russell held onto the lead but was caught by Verstappen, who quickly dispatched Gasly, and the Red Bull driver surprisingly had the speed to overtake Russell too.
While Verstappen defended hard from Russell, Antonelli was remarkably up to third as he overtook the Racing Bulls drivers, Piastri, title rivals Norris and Hamilton, plus Gasly to be in third after just 13 laps.
The field was bunched together so Antonelli joined the Verstappen, Russell scrap which turned into a Mercedes one-two as Verstappen struggled more on his tyres.
Mercedes wanted their drivers to help each other with the use of Overtake Mode - which allows more electrical deployment when a driver is within one second of the car in front.
After some back and forth, Russell and Antonelli slowly pulled away from Verstappen. But, the key moment came on Lap 29 as Stroll stopped with a reliability issue which caused a Virtual Safety Car.
Given Russell was on hard tyres, Mercedes elected to keep him out but Antonelli and Verstappen pitted as they were on mediums. However, post-race Russell stated he thought Antonelli was also going to stay out.
On fresh tyres, Antonelli again overtook Gasly, Norris, Hamilton and Piastri with ease, and was setting some blistering lap times to catch Russell.
A change for the lead late on felt inevitable but Antonelli was caught out by his first overtake attempt on Russell when he ran wide at Turn 2 which was breaking up due to the intense heat at Monza.
But, he got back onto Russell's tail after two laps and took the lead down to the Ascari Chicane with three laps remaining and went on to take a memorable victory.
"It was quite scary there in the moment [when I went wide]. The tarmac was breaking up but I still thought I could do the corner," he said.
"But once I went over a bit of gravel as well I went straight and I was like 'maybe I lost my chance'. But luckily we still had the pace and managed to bring it home."
