summary: London City Lionesses enter their second top-flight season aiming to break the established WSL order and reach the Champions League under billionaire owner Michele Kang. The club has heavily invested in a squad of seasoned international megastars, including Alexia Putellas, alongside improvements to infrastructure and commercial operations. However, manager Eder Maestre faces significant pressure to quickly unite the experienced roster and manage high financial operating losses without the backing of a men's club supporter base.
key_points: Billionaire owner Michele Kang aims to disrupt the traditional WSL top-three dominance and secure Champions League football.
The club has signed numerous high-profile, experienced international stars such as Alexia Putellas, Mary Earps, and Mapi León.
Financial strategy relies on initial owner investment transitioning into increased commercial revenue from sponsorships and ticket sales.
Manager Eder Maestre faces pressure to quickly build a cohesive team from a heavily altered, veteran-heavy squad.
London City lacks the built-in supporter pool of an established men's club, requiring creative marketing to draw large crowds.

title: Italian Grand Prix: George Russell leads Charles Leclerc in Friday practice at Monza
author: Andrew Benson
content:
![Mercedes' George Russell drives over a kerb during Italian Grand Prix first practice](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/7c26/live/f0af4d60-a870-11f1-bbad-43eaf67b94b6.jpg)
George Russell is 59 points behind Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli in the drivers' championship
- Published
Mercedes' George Russell topped Friday practice at the Italian Grand Prix from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.
Russell was 0.120 seconds quicker than Leclerc, with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who will start the race from the back with a grid penalty, just 0.021secs behind the Ferrari.
McLaren's Lando Norris was fourth fastest from the second Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton and McLaren's Oscar Piastri.
Red Bull's Max Verstappen, still yet to win a race this year, was 0.818secs off the pace with ninth-fastest time, behind the Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad and Oliver Bearman's Haas.
Ferrari have introduced an upgraded engine for this race but its performance will not be clear until qualifying and the race.
But the Italian team have lagged behind Mercedes on engine performance all season - Hamilton says they have regularly been losing 0.4secs on the straights - so to be as close as they were on a track which is so power-sensitive because of the amount of time spent at full throttle was encouraging on the face of it.
Antonelli's penalty is caused by using too many engine components this season after reliability problems earlier in the year. Russell will take one at a subsequent race, most likely the Azerbaijan Grand Prix later this month.
Mercedes have chosen this race because they hope the long straights will give him a decent chance of recovering a strong result.
And the Italian, who leads Hamilton and Russell in the championship by 59 points, was the quickest on the race-simulation runs towards the end of the session.
The race runs were inconclusive as Mercedes used the hard compound tyres, Ferrari the softs and Verstappen the mediums.
Antonelli was more than 0.2secs quicker than Russell on average. Norris, also on the hard tyre, was just under 0.2secs slower than Russell.
Meanwhile, F1 has announced that it will host a three-day event for fans before next season in Milan on 18-20 February.
A successor to the F1 Live event in London's O2 Arena in 2025, it will feature all 11 teams and their drivers as well as music and entertainment.
summary: Mercedes driver George Russell set the pace in Friday practice for the Italian Grand Prix at Monza, finishing just ahead of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli. Antonelli, who leads the drivers' championship, will start the race from the back due to a grid penalty for exceeding his engine component limit. Meanwhile, Formula 1 announced a three-day fan event to be held in Milan next February featuring all 11 teams and drivers.
key_points: George Russell topped the Friday practice session at Monza, 0.120 seconds faster than Charles Leclerc.
Kimi Antonelli will start the race from the back of the grid after receiving a penalty for using too many engine components.
Ferrari introduced an upgraded engine for the Italian Grand Prix.
Formula 1 announced a three-day fan event in Milan scheduled for February 18-20 featuring all 11 teams and drivers.

title: Gary Neville makes Arsenal vs Chelsea prediction
author: Bryan Nicholson
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Mikel Arteta press conference after Arsenal beat Aston Villa](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/21/22/01KZXNJ8EASFDYV5NFH9X82XM8.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
![Arsenal Football Newsletter](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_arsenal_embed_desktop.png)
Xabi Alonso’s new-look Blues side are looking to continue their perfect start to the season, while also putting down a marker in the Premier League title race. However, not to be outdone, the defending champions have also started the season with six points from a possible six.
And former Manchester United right-back Neville believes the weekend derby at the Emirates Stadium will be a very telling encounter for the remainder of the season.
Neville’s tipped Chelsea to be Arsenal’s biggest rivals to their league crown with a predicted second-placed finish, and feels the London derby will “show us where both teams are”.
But bragging rights should be claimed by Arsenal, who will edge a close encounter.
He said on The Overlap: “I think Arsenal will realise Chelsea have better attacking players than Aston Villa so they’ll have to be alert and alive.”
“They won’t defend in the same way as Villa so I think Arsenal may actually fancy their chances going forward more against Chelsea, but they’ll also have to be alert to the fact Chelsea have some fantastic attacking players.
“That’s what makes it really interesting.”
The eight-time Premier League winner made his score line prediction of “2-0 to Arsenal”, and added: “I think Arsenal are going to be so up for it.
“They are going to be really aggressive. I think Arsenal will win the game.”
Both sides look to have very different playing styles. Arsenal have kept two routine clean sheets in an easy 3-0 win against Coventry, and a 1-0 victory last time out against Aston Villa. Chelsea, meanwhile, look like they could be a thrilling watch this season with seven goals scored and five goals conceded in their two wins, while in both games playing for long periods without the ball.
summary: Former Manchester United player Gary Neville has predicted that Arsenal will defeat Chelsea 2-0 in their upcoming Premier League derby at the Emirates Stadium. Neville believes Chelsea, managed by Xabi Alonso, will be Arsenal's biggest rivals for the league title this season. He noted that the match will be a telling encounter that highlights the contrasting styles of both teams.
key_points: Gary Neville predicts a 2-0 victory for Arsenal against Chelsea.
Neville views Chelsea as Arsenal's biggest title rivals this season, tipping them for a second-place finish.
Arsenal has started the season with two clean sheets, while Chelsea has scored seven goals and conceded five.
Neville expects Arsenal to be highly aggressive and well-prepared for Chelsea's strong attacking players.

title: US Open 2026 results: Coco Gauff joins Naomi Osaka and Iga Swiatek in third round
author: Harry Poole
content:
![Coco Gauff clenches her fist and yells in celebration after beating Paula Badosa at the US Open](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/7e5f/live/5860d9b0-a7fe-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Coco Gauff won her first Grand Slam singles title at the 2023 US Open
- Published
A "battle-tested" Coco Gauff showed grit to keep her bid for a second US Open title alive with victory over Paula Badosa in the second round.
Fourth seed Gauff had lost her past two matches against Spanish former world number two Badosa, but showed impressive composure in a tough encounter at Flushing Meadows in New York.
American Gauff was twice a break up in the second set and served for the match at 6-5, only to put a volley into the net to send it to a tie-break.
After a quick yell of "why?" towards her team, Gauff reset and was solid to close out victory on a second match point.
Gauff's improved second serve was on show throughout - she won 57% of points behind it and committed only five double faults.
"I saw the draw - it is definitely not someone you want to play in the second round," Gauff, 22, said.
"But I need matches like this to build my confidence and I'm happy with how I managed today.
"Getting through in straight sets too makes a big difference. Yes, I was battle-tested, but I think it was a good battle where I wasn't out on the court for three hours."
Gauff would need to win the title and hope Elena Rybakina does not reach the semi-finals if she is to become world number one.
Kazakhstani second seed Rybakina claimed a 6-2 6-4 victory over Spain's Jessica Bouzas Maneiro, meaning the women's top 10 in the WTA rankings have reached the third round of a Grand Slam for the first time since Wimbledon in 2009.
![Naomi Osaka walks on to court wearing a white dress](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/94a0/live/10705e90-a7cd-11f1-809e-25fc74c1ec7d.jpg)
Naomi Osaka has become renowned for arriving at Grand Slam matches wearing eye-catching outfits
Osaka battles and Swiatek cruises
Earlier on Thursday, Naomi Osaka recovered from a second-set blip to overcome Czech Katerina Siniakova 6-2 5-7 6-1.
Two-time winner Osaka served for a place in the third round during the second set but lost four straight games as she squandered a 5-3 lead.
However, after leaving the court to reset, the Japanese 28-year-old overpowered top-ranked doubles player Siniakova in the decider.
After Osaka walked out for her first-round match in an outfit inspired by NBA legend Allen Iverson, she returned to the court on Thursday wearing a white dress embroidered with tennis racquets.
The 2018 and 2020 US Open winner took a commanding first set in half an hour, and looked on course for a straightforward victory after breaking serve for a 4-2 lead in the second.
That marked the start of four successive breaks of serve - including Osaka failing to close out the match - and Siniakova took full advantage as the 13th seed's consistency dipped.
But Osaka, who made 20 of her 29 unforced errors in the second set, returned to her former levels and won six of the final seven games to complete victory in two hours two minutes.
"The match was definitely really tough. I was a little bit too hard on myself after opportunities in the second set," Osaka told the crowd inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
"I took the bathroom break, regrouped a little, came back and just tried to have no regrets."
Poland's Iga Swiatek, a six-time major winner and former world number one whose sole US Open triumph arrived in 2022, beat Argentina's Nadia Podoroska 6-3 6-2 to set up a meeting with Czech Marie Bouzkova.
American former runner-up Madison Keys saved five match points to triumph 5-7 6-4 7-6 (10-5) in a thrilling match with Hungary's Anna Bondar.
summary: Coco Gauff defeated Paula Badosa in straight sets at the US Open to advance to the third round alongside Naomi Osaka and Iga Swiatek. Gauff showed composure after missing an opportunity to serve out the match in the second set, securing victory in a tie-break. Meanwhile, Osaka recovered from a second-set collapse against Katerina Siniakova to win in three sets, and Swiatek cruised past Nadia Podoroska.
key_points: Coco Gauff overcame Paula Badosa in straight sets to keep her bid for a second US Open title alive.
Naomi Osaka rebounded from a lost second-set lead to defeat Katerina Siniakova 6-2 5-7 6-1.
Iga Swiatek defeated Argentina's Nadia Podoroska 6-3 6-2 to reach the third round.
The advancement of the top 10 women in the WTA rankings marks the first time since Wimbledon in 2009 that all top 10 seeds reached the third round of a Grand Slam.

title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: London mayor Sadiq Khan wants fight at Wembley
author: Kal Sajad
content:
![Split image of Tyson Fury celebrating and Anthony Joshua pointing from ringside](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/0a8d/live/4d0eb030-7aba-11f1-9510-1546718f668b.png)
Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua are former two-time world heavyweight champions
- Published
London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.
BBC Sport understands Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium.
However, with organisers and broadcaster Netflix understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout, sources close to the discussions say talks over a London venue have not progressed, with no detailed talks over dates or timings.
"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.
Wembley Stadium's usual curfew is 23:00, although Khan has previously indicated he would support efforts to bring the fight to London.
A late-night fight in London - potentially in the early hours - could mean it draws a larger television audience in the US.
Brent Council, the local authority involved in any approval, has said a potential extension of the curfew would need to be assessed by Wembley's safety advisory group.
It remains unclear how late that curfew could be pushed back.
"Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are two great British boxers. Both have been world champions," Khan said.
"They both recognise and love the fans in this country who have supported them throughout their careers, amateur and professional.
"Wembley has hosted many fantastic events, including bouts involving Tyson and Anthony. We, the fans, want to see them box live in London."
There is hope that the venue will be finalised in the coming days. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has said he wants an announcement this week, with a news conference to follow next week.
BBC Sport has contacted Sela for comment.
Hearn says his side signed a contract for the bout to take place in the United Kingdom, while Sela and Netflix's preference would be the United States, to cater for American audiences.
Matchroom Boxing's Hearn has previously said Joshua's contract specifically stipulated a UK venue and would need to be renegotiated for the fight to take place Stateside.
Hearn says he has since set out terms under which Matchroom would agree to the change, with negotiations continuing over a possible move to New York.
The contact from Sela represents a significant development from the end of July, when sources close to the mayor told BBC Sport there had been no approach from the fight's organisers.
But the lack of progress since that initial contact underlines the uncertainty still surrounding Wembley's chances of hosting the contest.
"I'm hoping the promoters understand that not only will you get 100,000 people watching this bout live, you'll get millions watching it across the globe, where both boxers are cheered on by their loyal fans," Khan said.
AJ v Fury - highly anticipated or a forgotten fight?
summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan has expressed a strong desire to host the proposed boxing match between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua at Wembley Stadium. While Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office, organisers and broadcaster Netflix reportedly favor New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn states that a UK venue is stipulated in the current contract, and negotiations are ongoing regarding a potential move to the United States.
key_points: London Mayor Sadiq Khan wants Wembley Stadium to host the Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua fight.
Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office about bringing the bout to London.
Organisers and broadcaster Netflix reportedly prefer New York's Madison Square Garden for the November fight.
Eddie Hearn says Joshua's contract specifies a UK venue, which would require renegotiation for a US bout.
Hosting the fight in London could involve navigating Wembley's standard 23:00 curfew and local safety approvals.

title: Richarlison: Tottenham omit Brazil forward from Premier League squad
author: Sami Mokbel
content:
![Brazil forward Richarlison](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/8b4f/live/74ac0e50-a7b8-11f1-b5cf-8556ae508a51.jpg)
Richarlison joined Tottenham from Everton in the summer of 2022
- Published
Richarlison has been left out of Tottenham's Premier League squad.
Spurs manager Roberto de Zerbi said last week the Brazil forward had asked to leave the club and he looked close to joining former club Everton before Tuesday's transfer deadline, but a deal fell through.
The 29-year-old has now been left out the club's squad to play in top-flight games for the first half of the season.
It is understood Richarlison does not feature in Tottenham's plans this season, which was explained to the player before Tuesday's deadline.
He is expected to leave the club in the coming days, with the transfer windows in Turkey and Saudi Arabia still open.
Richarlison joined Tottenham from Everton in the summer of 2022, having joined the Toffees from Watford in 2018.
He has entered the final year of his contract at the London club and, while he started Tottenham's defeat by Brentford in their opening game of the Premier League season, he was not included in De Zerbi's squad when Spurs lost 2-0 at home to Newcastle United on Saturday.
After the game, De Zerbi said: "Richarlison, I don't know. He said too many times he wants to leave."
Earlier in August, the Spurs boss said that the Brazilian was uncertain about his future, noting that "it's not easy to find another striker like Richarlison".
However, Spurs recently signed Manchester City striker Omar Marmoush on loan and he replaced Richarlison against Newcastle.
Richarlison was Tottenham's top scorer in the league last season with 11 goals in 32 appearances and also provided four assists as he was a key figure during their struggle for Premier League survival, which was secured on the final day.
summary: Tottenham Hotspur has omitted Brazil forward Richarlison from their Premier League squad for the first half of the season. Manager Roberto de Zerbi stated that Richarlison repeatedly expressed a desire to leave, and a potential deadline-day move to Everton fell through. Richarlison is now expected to depart the club in the coming days with transfer windows still open in Turkey and Saudi Arabia.
key_points: Richarlison was left out of Tottenham's Premier League squad.
Manager Roberto de Zerbi stated the forward had asked to leave the club.
A close transfer deal to former club Everton fell through before the deadline.
Richarlison is expected to leave as transfer windows remain open in Turkey and Saudi Arabia.
Tottenham recently signed striker Omar Marmoush on loan.

title: Italian Grand Prix at Monza declared heat-hazard race by FIA
author: Andrew Benson
content:
![Ferrari's Charles Leclerc arrives at the Monza paddock on media day for the Italian Grand Prix](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/7f73/live/7737f280-a77a-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc has twice won the Italian Grand Prix, in 2019 and 2024
- Published
The Italian Grand Prix has been declared a heat-hazard race as high temperatures continue in the country following the summer heatwave.
A heat hazard is an official designation for an event where it is forecasted that temperatures will be more than 31C at some point during the race on Sunday.
The ambient temperatures around Monza, north-east of Milan, are expected to be in the mid-30C region all weekend.
They peaked at 36C on Wednesday afternoon near Milan's Linate airport.
The ruling means drivers can use a system that flows cooled liquid, such as glycol, through a system of pipes in a fireproof top worn under their overalls.
The cooling kit is not mandatory, but any driver who chooses not to use it has to carry 5kg of ballast in their car to ensure they do not have a competitive advantage.
Italy is the second race this year to be declared a heat hazard. The first was Austria early in the summer heatwave.
Some drivers prefer not to use the cooling kit because of discomfort, and because there have been issues with the coolant running out before a grand prix is finished.
In that case, the liquid ends up at car temperature, which is considerably higher than ambient.
Temperatures in the cockpit of an F1 car can be more than 40C, and drivers are wearing several layers of fireproof clothing in addition to a balaclava and helmet, so overheating is a serious concern.
summary: The FIA has declared the Italian Grand Prix at Monza a heat-hazard race due to forecasted temperatures exceeding 31C. This designation allows drivers to wear a liquid-cooled garment under their fireproof overalls to combat cockpit temperatures that can surpass 40C. While optional, drivers who choose not to use the cooling system must carry 5kg of ballast in their cars.
key_points: The Italian Grand Prix at Monza is officially designated as a heat-hazard race.
Ambient temperatures around Monza are expected to reach the mid-30C region over the weekend.
The ruling permits drivers to use a liquid-cooled garment under their racing overalls to prevent overheating.
Drivers who opt out of using the cooling kit must carry an additional 5kg of ballast in their car.
Cockpit temperatures in F1 cars can exceed 40C, creating serious risks of driver overheating.

title: US Open 2026 results: Aryna Sabalenka continues title defence with one of the quickest Grand Slam wins of her career
author: Jonathan Jurejko
content:
![Aryna Sabalenka blows a kiss to the US Open crowd](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/28ee/live/98c7d600-a733-11f1-b2fc-b90b4b6e44c1.jpg)
Aryna Sabalenka is bidding to become only the third woman to win three successive US Open titles, following Chris Evert (1975-78) and Serena Williams (2012-2014)
- Published
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka earned one of the quickest Grand Slam wins of her career with a 53-minute pummelling of US Open debutant Polina Iatcenko in the second round.
However, the world number one did not look entirely happy even as she swept aside Iatcenko - then had a spiky exchange with a reporter in her post-match news conference.
Sabalenka took umbrage with what she perceived to be a suggestion from a reporter that she had been attending "lots of parties" in the build-up to the US Open.
"What kind of question is that? Just because I posted some activities with brands, you think that I've been partying [and] not training?" countered Sabalenka.
Asked if she was "getting serious" now the tournament was under way, she said: "Oh yeah, I wasn't serious before that. Next question."
Sabalenka, 28, is aiming to win her first major title of a strange season where she has enjoyed spectacular success but is now looking to recover from a recent dip.
Coasting to a 6-1 6-1 victory over 22-year-old qualifier Iatcenko did not offer a true test of where Sabalenka's level is.
But the ruthless manner in which she secured victory will certainly boost confidence as she looks to complete a rare 'three-peat' of US Open titles.
"I'm happy with the level I played, happy with the focus and happy to be through this match," said Sabalenka, who will play Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova in the third round.
Sabalenka hits out at 'joke' journalist after question over partying
Sabalenka knows she must the lift the trophy in New York again to stand any chance of preventing Elena Rybakina taking her position at the top of the rankings.
Even if Sabalenka does retain the title, Rybakina would still rise to the summit by reaching the semi-finals.
Sabalenka losing the top spot seemed unthinkable after a storming start to the season, reaching the Australian Open final and winning the Indian Wells and Miami titles back-to-back.
Losing to Rybakina in Melbourne was Sabalenka's only defeat in her first 27 matches of 2026. After completing the Sunshine Double, her win-loss record leading into the US Open dropped to 17-7 and she has only reached one WTA semi-final in the past five months.
Before the final Grand Slam of the season, Sabalenka admitted she had been "dealing with several things" in a period which she knows was far below her best.
Sabalenka's pace and power was too much for world number 160 Iatcenko, who managed just three winners compared to the 24 put away by the top seed.
Iatcenko looked a bundle of nerves in the biggest match of her career, but composed herself to get on the scoreboard for 5-1 and immediately broke out into a relieved smile.
It was merely respite as Sabalenka held to love in fewer than 90 seconds to clinch the opening set.
Despite only being on court for 24 minutes, Iatchenko decided she wanted a bathroom break to change her kit - but more likely for a mental reset than anything else.
Sabalenka kept loose while she waited by practising her serves and maintained her rhythm as she surged a double break ahead for 3-0 in the second set.
It was not all plain-sailing for Sabalenka as she lost serve in a sloppy fourth game, but reasserted her authority with two more breaks as Iatchenko was taught a harsh lesson.
The Russian can console herself with the knowledge she has gained valuable experience against the world number one on the biggest court on the planet - and a bumper paycheck.
Coming into the US Open, she had earned $300,000 (Â£220,000) in her career but takes another $190,000 home from New York to reinvest into her future.
Earlier on Wednesday, third seed Pegula continued her quest for a maiden Grand Slam singles title with a comfortable victory over fellow American Sofia Kenin.
Pegula also has a shot of replacing Sabalenka as world number one if she wins the title, as does fourth seed Coco Gauff, and kept her dream alive with a 6-3 6-1 win.
There were also straight-set wins for Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, SW19 runner-up Karolina Muchova, two-time major semi-finalist Marta Kostyuk and teenage American sensation Iva Jovic as the pattern of few shocks in the women's draw over the opening two rounds continued.
summary: Defending champion Aryna Sabalenka advanced to the third round of the US Open with a quick 53-minute victory over qualifier Polina Iatcenko. Despite the dominant win, Sabalenka had a tense post-match news conference after taking issue with a reporter's question about her preparation. She is bidding to become only the third woman to win three successive US Open titles.
key_points: Aryna Sabalenka defeated Polina Iatcenko 6-1 6-1 in just 53 minutes during the second round.
Sabalenka had a spiky exchange with a journalist in her post-match news conference regarding her pre-tournament activities.
The world number one is attempting to secure her third consecutive US Open title.
Sabalenka will face Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova in the next round.

title: Man City transfer news: New midfield but major Haaland gamble
author: Shamoon Hafez; Umir Irfan
content:
![Elliot Anderson (left), Enzo Fernandez (middle) and Ayyoub Bouaddi](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/dfdf/live/8babcca0-a6cb-11f1-b0c9-07afcdd8053c.png)
Elliot Anderson (left), Enzo Fernandez (middle) and Ayyoub Bouaddi have cost a combined Â£327m for Manchester City this summer
- Published
Manchester City have completed their squad overhaul - including a fully revamped midfield - to the tune of Â£458m, a new Premier League record for a summer window.
But that eyewatering sum does not tell the full story.
New Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca received the full backing of director of football Hugo Viana in his first transfer window in charge after replacing Pep Guardiola. Indeed, City's record transfer fee was twice broken this summer.
A joint-British record Â£125m was spent on Maresca's former Chelsea skipper Enzo Fernandez after Â£116m was committed on Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest. Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, was also brought in for Â£86m. The trio accounted for the bulk of City's summer incomings.
The departures of captain Bernardo Silva, 2024 Ballon d'Or winner Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez means the City midfield has been completely transformed.
Senior club sources are said to be delighted by the business done not only during the past couple of months but in January too, when plans were brought forward to sign long-term targets Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi.
And if the clock is rewound further back, Manchester City's rebuild of the team that won the 2023 Champions League really began in January 2025 after a difficult start to that season.
Just four players remain from the starting eleven and substitutes from the night they beat Inter Milan in Istanbul to win the continent's biggest club prize.
Maresca now has the luxury of calling upon two established players in almost every position. City feel the squad is stronger at this point than at the beginning of last season which they believe has been achieved by remaining calm and trusting the transfer strategy.
However some big questions remain.
How will their new midfield signings all fit together?
And, despite the vast amount of money spent, have they actually left themselves without a back-up to Erling Haaland?
Selection dilemmas for Maresca
![Manchester City squad depth this season](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/921a/live/9655b040-a701-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.png)
City's expenditure of Â£542m on new signings since the turn of the year will grab the headlines, but it often goes under the radar how well they do at selling fringe players.
During this same period, they have recouped Â£334m, including Â£75m for Savinho, who scored only two Premier League goals during his time at City, as well as Â£65m for Rodri and Â£52m for Reijnders.
It gives City a net spend of Â£208m in 2026, which will be further bolstered by Tottenham's obligation to buy Omar Marmoush for Â£60m at the end of his loan spell next season.
Sources had said during the summer that they were operating on a one-out, one-in policy and Maresca managed to replace almost every player that departed, aside from Nico Gonzalez and Marmoush.
With the side well stocked at left-back, it is felt that Nico O'Reilly will play more in his natural midfield position to ease the Gonzalez gap.
The club believe the record fee for Fernandez is justified by acquiring a proven winner at the highest level that will strengthen the midfield. Anderson was the summer's number one target, while 18-year-old Bouaddi is seen as having all the attributes to develop into a world class talent.
City have won back-to-back games at the start of the Premier League season and Maresca will now have a selection dilemma each game as he possesses an embarrassment of riches to choose from.
The question is how the Italian will now fit them all together.
Analysis: How will Maresca use his new midfielders?
Fernandez, Bouaddi, and Anderson are all players comfortable across multiple positions in Maresca's system.
Maresca has moved between a box and a diamond shape in midfield at City. The main difference between the two shapes is that the former has two natural holding midfielders and the second a single holding midfielder.
Against Bournemouth, Guehi paired Anderson at the base of midfield. O'Reilly, the left-sided attacking midfielder, was joined by right-back Rico Lewis, moving in-field to form the box.
Against Crystal Palace, left-back Josko Gvardiol and attacking midfielder O'Reilly flanked number 10 Rayan Cherki as the three ahead of Anderson in what looked like a diamond.
- ![A screen grab from Manchester City against Bournemouth illustrating their box shape in midfield.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/245c/live/fd70af10-a624-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.png) Image caption, Manchester City used a box midfield against Bournemouth.
1 of 2
Anderson anchoring the midfield suggests Maresca sees him as Rodri's successor.
While full of praise for Bouaddi, Maresca has stressed his youth, a nod to the fact that he will likely deputise for Anderson.
Bouaddi replaced Anderson against Palace and his short cameo came soon after the introduction of Mateo Kovacic. In pre-season, the Croatian appeared to be Maresca's first choice holding midfielder but has since slid down the pecking order.
When he came on, although starting higher than Bouaddi in the midfield diamond, he dropped deep to get on the ball in holding midfield. When this happened, Bouaddi took Kovacic's position higher up.
These rotations between holding midfield and central midfield are movements Maresca may also encourage Anderson to perform when others fill the space behind him.
- ![A screen grab from Manchester City against Crystal Palace illustrating their midfield shape focusing on the positions of Mateo Kovacic and Ayyoub Bouaddi.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/bb67/live/8d4312e0-a625-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.png) Image caption, When Bouaddi came on, he took up a holding midfield position, particularly in deep build-up play. Kovacic was positioned ahead of him as the right central midfielder.
1 of 2
Versatility in the midfield four is key. Fernandez, under Maresca, was capable of playing at the base of midfield or as an attacking midfielder on both sides.
The last midfield spot, the number 10 position, has been shared between Foden and Cherki. Although Foden did play right wing against Bournemouth and Palace given City's injuries, Maresca has spoken of his central quality.
Given Foden's promising showings as a box-to-box midfielder last season â there is also a possibility both him and Cherki play through the middle together at some point this season.
But....a lack of back-up for Haaland?
Despite the positives around the recent window, Haaland is now City's only first-team striker.
The 26-year-old is pivotal to the team, ending last season as the Premier League top scorer with 27 goals, and starting the new campaign by netting twice in as many games.
But should Haaland be unavailable, what are City's options?
Marmoush wanted to play regular first-team football and was allowed to join Tottenham, while 21-year-old Divin Mubama, who did well in pre-season, joined Championship side Southampton on loan.
City believe they have enough flexibility from within their options to have not directly replaced Marmoush.
Semenyo operates mainly from the right flank but is seen as an option at number nine, having played in the position during some cup games last season.
Deadline day signing Ndiaye is another who can operate there and the Â£60m forward adds greater versatility and squad depth as someone who is a proven Premier League player.
However, of the forward, attacking midfield and wide options, Semenyo is the only one to get into double figures in the Premier League in the last couple of seasons.
Cherki, Jeremy Doku and Ndiaye have never hit that mark, while Foden is clearly capable, having hit 19 Premier League goals in 2023-24, but has struggled for consistent form in the last two seasons
Unless a couple of those step up, it could be one to watch if Haaland either needs to be rested or gets injured.
summary: Manchester City broke the Premier League summer transfer window record by spending £458m under new manager Enzo Maresca, entirely revamping their midfield with arrivals like Enzo Fernandez, Elliot Anderson, and Ayyoub Bouaddi. Despite strong player sales resulting in a net spend of £208m since the turn of the year, questions remain about how the new midfield will gel and whether the club has left itself without adequate back-up for star striker Erling Haaland. Maresca now faces selection dilemmas as he works to integrate his versatile new squad following departures such as Rodri and Bernardo Silva.
key_points: Manchester City spent a record £458m in the summer transfer window, bringing their total expenditure since the turn of the year to £542m.
Major midfield signings included Enzo Fernandez (£125m), Elliot Anderson (£116m), and Ayyoub Bouaddi (£86m) following departures like Rodri and Bernardo Silva.
City recouped £334m from selling fringe players during the same period, leading to a net spend of £208m.
Concerns remain over whether City lacks a direct, proven back-up striker for Erling Haaland after letting Omar Marmoush and Divin Mubama leave.

title: US Open 2026 results: Katie Boulter wins just one game in 58-minute US Open defeat by Karolina Muchova
author: Emily Salley
content:
![Katie Boulter](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/7f6c/live/06d61040-a715-11f1-8596-77a4bf645971.jpg)
Katie Boulter has won just two Grand Slam matches this year
- Published
British number one Katie Boulter endured a "bad day at the office" as she won just one game in a 58-minute demolition by Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova in the US Open second round.
The match, originally scheduled to be played on one of the outer courts, was moved to the 14,000-capacity Louis Armstrong Stadium after heavy rain in New York.
But fans who had counted themselves lucky to have gained a third match on their day session ticket may have been left feeling short-changed, as Boulter fell to a swift 6-1 6-0 defeat by the Czech seventh seed.
"Ultimately, it was a bad day at the office â times two," said Boulter.
"I struggled with the conditions. I struggled with the roof, the noise, I let things distract me.
"I let it get to me. I'm not usually aware of everything going on. It made me feel a little bit uncomfortable. I have to deal with it better."
Fellow Britons Jacob Fearnley and Toby Samuel failed to reach the men's third round on Wednesday, both losing to seeded players in Argentina's Tomas Martin Etcheverry and Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic.
But Francesca Jones had better fortune as she returned to win her first-round match against Poland's Magda Linette after it was interrupted by rain on Tuesday.
Boulter's serve let her down as she hit eight double faults and no aces, while she won just 33% of points behind her first serve.
Unable to fend off any of the seven break points she faced, the 30-year-old was not helped by an unforced error count of 22 compared to just four winners.
In comparison, two-time US Open semi-finalist Muchova landed 14 winners and just nine unforced errors as she impressed with smart drop shots and piercing groundstrokes.
"I would be really humbled [if I was Boulter], I would sit down with my team and say 'OK, we need to change something big time'," former world number five Daniela Hantuchova told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"First of all, it was very obvious today that it was the serve. I feel like it needs to be cleared up because she was losing the rhythm and not using her legs. That's the number one thing.
"If I am Boulter, I would be on the practice court tomorrow. If she still wants to invest everything into her tennis then she needs to be on the court."
Boulter has had plenty to celebrate in her personal life this summer after marrying Australia's Alex de Minaur, the world number seven, in July.
However, it has been a disappointing tennis season for the world number 62, with just two wins across the four Grand Slam tournaments.
Since suffering a first-round exit at Wimbledon, Boulter has won just two of the six matches she has played.
Jones 'shows northern grit' in win
![Fran Jones](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/f739/live/fd4f7520-a719-11f1-8596-77a4bf645971.jpg)
Jones won her first Grand Slam match at the French Open earlier this year
Jones had won the first set 6-4 against Linette, ranked 82nd, when the rain put a halt to proceedings on Tuesday night.
When the pair returned on Wednesday, it was Linette who appeared fresher as she raced to a 5-0 lead and wrapped up the second set in 28 minutes.
"I've never been quite in this position so I was nervous with how I'd quite feel about coming back out," Jones told Sky Sports afterwards.
"I thought I'd maybe handle it better than the score reflects."
Jones rallied back in the decider, claiming the decisive break at 2-1 before completing the victory - just her second at Grand Slam level.
She will play American 14th seed Iva Jovic in the second round on Thursday.
"[I'm] really grateful that I just managed to pull through," said Jones.
"She came out all guns blazing - it was incredible how she was playing until about 4-0 and then it started to equal out. But in that situation, hats off if they can sustain that, I just tried to show my northern grit, stick in there and do what I can."
Fearnley had produced a remarkable five-set comeback against Spain's Martin Landaluce in the first round, but the British lucky loser's fortune ran out in a 6-3 6-3 3-6 6-3 defeat by against Etcheverry.
The Argentine 27th seed recovered from losing the third set and falling a break behind in the fourth, while Fearnley's 57 unforced errors and 11 double faults ultimately proved costly.
Samuel, 23, won through qualifying to reach round two on his US Open debut, but was beaten 6-4 6-2 6-4 by 18th seed Lehecka.
Meanwhile, British number three Jan Choinski fell to a 6-3 6-1 7-6 (7-5) defeat by Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp in a first-round match that had also been pushed back to Wednesday because of the rain.
summary: British number one Katie Boulter suffered a swift 6-1 6-0 defeat to Karolina Muchova in the second round of the US Open, winning just one game in 58 minutes. Boulter admitted she struggled with the conditions and noise after the match was moved to Louis Armstrong Stadium due to rain. In other British singles action, Francesca Jones advanced to the second round following a rain-delayed win against Magda Linette, while Jacob Fearnley, Toby Samuel, and Jan Choinski all exited the tournament.
key_points: Katie Boulter lost 6-1 6-0 to Karolina Muchova in a 58-minute US Open second-round match.
The match was relocated to the Louis Armstrong Stadium due to heavy rain in New York.
Boulter committed eight double faults and 22 unforced errors during the lopsided defeat.
Fellow Briton Francesca Jones secured a rain-delayed first-round victory against Magda Linette.
British players Jacob Fearnley, Toby Samuel, and Jan Choinski were all eliminated in their respective matches.
